Another name for Cesarean Delivery. A cesarean delivery, also called a cesarean section or c-section, is surgery to deliver a baby. The baby is taken out through your abdomen (belly).
Another name for Cystic Fibrosis. Cystic fibrosis (CF) is an inherited disease of the mucus and sweat glands. It affects mostly your lungs, pancreas, liver, intestines, sinuses, and sex organs.

Another name for Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome. Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a serious, long-term illness that affects many body systems. Another name for it is chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS).

Chagas disease, or American trypanosomiasis, is an illness that can cause serious heart and stomach problems. It is caused by a parasite. Chagas disease is common in Latin America, especially in poor, rural areas.
Another name for Methamphetamine. Methamphetamine - meth for short - is a very addictive stimulant drug. It is a powder that can be made into a pill or a shiny rock (called a crystal).

Another name for Menopause. Menopause is the time in your life when you stop having your period and can no longer get pregnant. You have reached menopause when you have not had a period for 12 months.
Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT) is a group of genetic nerve disorders. It is named after the three doctors who first identified it. In the United States, CMT affects about 1 in 2,500 people.
Free or reduced-cost care that many hospitals offer to people with low income. Ask the hospital's billing office for an application.
Another name for Muscle Cramps. Muscle cramps are sudden, involuntary contractions or spasms in one or more of your muscles. They are very common and often occur after exercise.
When a hazardous chemical has been released, it may harm people's health. Chemical releases can be unintentional, as in the case of an industrial accident.
Strong medicines that kill cancer cells or stop them from growing. Side effects can include hair loss, nausea and tiredness.
Another name for Acute Bronchitis. Bronchitis is an inflammation of the bronchial tubes, the airways that carry air to your lungs. It causes a cough that often brings up mucus.
The chest is the part of your body between your neck and your abdomen (belly). The medical term for your chest is thorax.
Pain, pressure, squeezing or tightness in the chest. It can be a sign of a heart attack: call 911 if it is sudden, severe or spreads to the arm, jaw or back.
Another name for Smokeless Tobacco. Recent research shows the dangers of smokeless tobacco may go beyond the mouth. It might also play a role in other cancers, heart disease and stroke.

Another name for Heart Failure. Heart failure means that your heart can't pump enough oxygen-rich blood to meet your body's needs. Heart failure doesn't mean that your heart has stopped or is about to stop beating.
Doctors diagnose CM using imaging tests. Medicines may ease some symptoms, such as pain. Surgery is the only treatment available to correct or stop the progression of nerve damage.
A very contagious virus that causes an itchy rash of blisters. A vaccine prevents it.
Chikungunya is a virus that spread by the same kinds of mosquitoes that spread dengue and Zika virus. Rarely, the virus can spread from the pregnant parent to their newborn around the time of birth.
Child abuse is doing something or failing to do something that results in harm to a child or puts a child at risk of harm. Child abuse can be physical, sexual or emotional.
All kids misbehave some times. And some may have temporary behavior problems due to stress. For example, the birth of a sibling, a divorce, or a death in the family may cause a child to act out.
Healthy teeth are important to your child's overall health. From the time your child is born, there are things you can do to promote healthy teeth and prevent cavities.
As children grow older, they develop in several different ways. Child development includes physical, intellectual, social, and emotional changes.
It's important to recognize and treat mental illnesses in children early on. Once mental illness develops, it becomes a regular part of your child's behavior.
Learn about your children's nutrient requirements. Some of them, such as the requirements for iron and calcium, change as your child ages.
Sexual abuse is one form of child abuse. It includes a wide range of actions between a child and an adult or older child. Often these involve body contact, but not always.

Childbirth is the process of giving birth to a baby. It includes labor and delivery of the fetus and the placenta. The placenta is the organ that supplies food and oxygen through the umbilical cord to your fetus during pregnancy.

If you have problems in childbirth, your health care provider may need to give you medicines to induce or speed up labor, use tools to help guide the baby out of the birth canal, or deliver the baby by Cesarean section.
Another name for Juvenile Arthritis. Juvenile arthritis (JA) is arthritis that happens in children. It causes joint inflammation (swelling), pain, stiffness, and loss of motion.

Another name for Asthma in Children. Asthma is a chronic (long-term) lung disease. It affects your airways, the tubes that carry air in and out of your lungs. When you have asthma, your airways can become inflamed and narrowed.
Brain tumors are abnormal growths inside the skull. They are among the most common types of childhood cancers. Some are benign tumors, which aren't cancer.
When you have leukemia, your bone marrow makes large numbers of abnormal cells. This problem most often happens with white blood cells. These abnormal cells build up in your bone marrow and blood.
Vaccines are injections (shots), liquids, pills, or nasal sprays that you take to teach the immune system to recognize and defend against harmful germs.

Your child's health includes physical, mental and social well-being. Most parents know the basics of keeping children healthy, like offering them healthy foods, making sure they get enough sleep and exercise and ensuring their safety.
Feeling cold and shivering, often with a fever.
Children's Health Insurance Program: low-cost health coverage for children in families that earn too much for Medicaid but cannot afford private insurance.
Many people visit chiropractors for treatment of low back pain, neck pain, and headaches.
A practitioner who treats back, neck and joint pain, mainly by adjusting the spine.

Another name for Heroin. Heroin is an illegal, very addictive opioid drug. It's made from morphine, which comes from the seedpod of opium poppy plants. These plants grow in Southeast and Southwest Asia, Mexico, and Colombia.
Chlamydia is a common sexually transmitted infection (STI). It is caused by bacteria called Chlamydia trachomatis. Anyone can get chlamydia.
When something blocks the airway so a person cannot breathe, cough or speak. Call 911 and give abdominal thrusts (the Heimlich maneuver).

Another name for Bile Duct Cancer. Your liver makes a digestive juice called bile. Your gallbladder stores it between meals. When you eat, your gallbladder pushes the bile into tubes called bile ducts.
Another name for Vitamin D. You can get vitamin D in three ways: through your skin, from your diet, and from supplements. Your body forms vitamin D naturally after exposure to sunlight.
Surgery to take out the gallbladder, often because of gallstones.

Another name for Gallstones. Your gallbladder is a pear-shaped organ under your liver. It stores bile, a fluid made by your liver to digest fat. As your stomach and intestines digest food, your gallbladder releases bile through a tube called the common bile duct.
Cholera is a bacterial infection that causes diarrhea. The cholera bacterium is usually found in water or food that has been contaminated by feces (poop).
A fatty substance in the blood. Too much 'bad' cholesterol (LDL) can clog arteries and raise the risk of heart disease.

term: Cholesterol Levels: What You Need to Know
meaning: Cholesterol is a waxy, fat-like substance that's found in all the cells in your body. Your body needs some cholesterol to work properly. But if you have too much of it in your blood, it can stick to the walls of your arteries and narrow or even block them.

term: Choosing a Doctor or Health Care Service
meaning: On this page you'll find information to help you choose a health care provider or service.
Another name for Hemophilia. Hemophilia is a rare bleeding disorder in which the blood does not clot properly. This can lead to problems with bleeding too much after an injury or surgery.
Lasting a long time or coming back often, like diabetes or arthritis. The opposite of acute.
Chronic bronchitis is a type of COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). COPD is a group of lung diseases that make it hard to breathe and get worse over time.
Another name for Long COVID. There are several other names for long COVID. It can also be called post-COVID conditions, long-haul COVID, and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC).

Another name for Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome. Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a serious, long-term illness that affects many body systems. Another name for it is chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS).

Another name for Chronic Myeloid Leukemia. When you have leukemia, your bone marrow makes large numbers of abnormal cells. This problem most often happens with white blood cells. These abnormal cells build up in your bone marrow and blood.
Long-term damage that slowly makes the kidneys work less well (CKD). Diabetes and high blood pressure are the most common causes.

Pain is a signal from your nervous system that something may be wrong. It is an unpleasant feeling, such as a prick, tingle, sting, burn, or ache.

Another name for Scars. A scar is a permanent patch of skin that grows over a wound. It forms when your body heals itself after a cut, scrape, burn, or sore. You can also get scars from surgery that cuts through the skin, infections like chickenpox, or skin conditions like acne.

Another name for Smoking. There's no way around it; smoking is bad for your health. It harms nearly every organ of the body, even some that you would not expect. Cigarette smoking causes many cancers and other health problems.

Circumcision is a surgical procedure to remove the foreskin from the penis. The foreskin is the loose skin that covers the tip of the penis.
Another name for Scleroderma. Scleroderma means "hard skin." It's the name of an autoimmune disease that causes inflammation and thickening in the skin and other areas of the body.
Severe scarring of the liver from long-term damage, such as heavy drinking or hepatitis. The liver stops working well.

Another name for Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease. Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) is a rare, degenerative brain disorder. Symptoms usually start around age 60. Memory problems, behavior changes, vision problems, and poor muscle coordination progress quickly to dementia, coma, and death.
Another name for Chronic Kidney Disease. You have two kidneys, each about the size of your fist. Their main job is to filter your blood. They remove wastes and extra water, which become urine.
A request to your insurance company to pay for a health service you received.
Germs are a part of everyday life. Some of them are helpful, but others are harmful and cause disease. They can be found everywhere - in our air, soil, and water.
Cleft lip and cleft palate are birth defects that occur when a baby's lip or mouth do not form properly. They happen early during pregnancy.

Another name for Spina Bifida. Spina bifida is a neural tube defect - a type of birth defect of the brain, spine, or spinal cord. It happens if the spinal column of the fetus doesn't close completely during the first month of pregnancy.
Climate is the average weather in a place over a period of time. Climate change is major change in temperature, rainfall, snow, or wind patterns lasting for many years.
A place to get medical care without staying overnight.

Another name for Depression. Depression is more than a feeling of being sad or irritable for a few days. It's a serious mood disorder. As one of the most common mental disorders in the United States, depression can affect how you think, feel, and your everyday life.

Clinical trials are research studies that test how well new medical approaches work in people. Each study answers scientific questions and tries to find better ways to prevent, screen for, diagnose, or treat a disease.

Another name for Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia. When you have leukemia, your bone marrow makes large numbers of abnormal cells. This problem most often happens with white blood cells. These abnormal cells build up in your bone marrow and blood.

Cloning describes the processes used to create an exact genetic replica of another cell, tissue or organism. The copied material, which has the same genetic makeup as the original, is referred to as a clone.
An antiplatelet medicine (brand name Plavix) that helps prevent clots, often after a stent.

Another name for C. diff Infections. C. diff is a bacterium that can cause diarrhea and more serious intestinal conditions such as colitis. You may see it called other names, such as Clostridioides difficile (the new name), Clostridium difficile (an older name), and C. difficile.

Another name for C. diff Infections. C. diff is a bacterium that can cause diarrhea and more serious intestinal conditions such as colitis. You may see it called other names, such as Clostridioides difficile (the new name), Clostridium difficile (an older name), and C. difficile.

Another name for C. diff Infections. C. diff is a bacterium that can cause diarrhea and more serious intestinal conditions such as colitis. You may see it called other names, such as Clostridioides difficile (the new name), Clostridium difficile (an older name), and C. difficile.

Another name for Bleeding Disorders. Normally, if you get hurt, your body forms a blood clot to stop the bleeding. For blood to clot, your body needs cells called platelets and proteins known as clotting factors.
Club drugs are a group of psychoactive drugs. They act on the central nervous system and can cause changes in mood, awareness, and behavior.

Another name for Chronic Myeloid Leukemia. When you have leukemia, your bone marrow makes large numbers of abnormal cells. This problem most often happens with white blood cells. These abnormal cells build up in your bone marrow and blood.
Another name for Cytomegalovirus Infections. Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is a virus found around the world. It is related to the viruses that cause chickenpox and infectious mononucleosis (mono).

Another name for Carbon Monoxide Poisoning. It is often hard to tell if someone has CO poisoning, because the symptoms may be like those of other illnesses. People who are sleeping or intoxicated can die from CO poisoning before they have symptoms.

Another name for Cocaine. Cocaine is a very addictive drug that is made from leaves of the coca plant found in South America. It is mostly available as an illegal drug that some people use to get high.

Another name for Valley Fever. Valley Fever is a disease caused by a fungus (or mold) called Coccidioides. The fungi live in the soil of dry areas like the southwestern U.S.
Another name for Tailbone Disorders. The tailbone is the small bone at the bottom of your backbone, or spine. Tailbone disorders include tailbone injuries, pain, infections, cysts and tumors.
A cochlear implant is a small, complex electronic device that can help to provide a sense of sound. People who are profoundly deaf or severely hard-of-hearing can get help from them.
A type of talk therapy (CBT) that helps you notice and change unhelpful thoughts and habits.
Problems with memory, thinking or decision-making that are more than normal for a person's age.
The percentage of a bill you pay after you have met your deductible. For example, with 20% coinsurance you pay $20 of a $100 bill.

Another name for Cocaine. Cocaine is a very addictive drug that is made from leaves of the coca plant found in South America. It is mostly available as an illegal drug that some people use to get high.
Cold and cough medicines can help relieve symptoms of a common cold. The symptoms of a cold can include a sore throat, stuffy or runny nose, sneezing, and coughing.
A small, painful blister on or near the lips caused by a virus. Also called a fever blister.
Cold sores are caused by a contagious virus called herpes simplex virus (HSV). There are two types of HSV. Type 1 usually causes oral herpes, or cold sores.

Another name for Hypothermia. Cold weather can affect your body in different ways. You can get frostbite, which is an injury to the body that is caused by freezing. Your body can also lose heat faster than you can produce it.
Long periods of crying in a healthy baby, often in the evening, for no clear reason. It usually gets better by 3 to 4 months.

Another name for Ulcerative Colitis. Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a disease that causes inflammation and sores, called ulcers, in the lining of the rectum and colon. It is one of a group of diseases called inflammatory bowel disease.
A collapsed lung happens when air enters the pleural space, the area between the lung and the chest wall. If it is a total collapse, it is called pneumothorax.
College life involves excitement, along with new challenges, risks, and responsibilities. You are meeting new people, learning new things, and making your own decisions.
The large intestine: the last part of the digestive tract, which absorbs water and forms stool.

Another name for Colorectal Cancer. Cancer that begins in the colon is called colon cancer, and cancer that begins in the rectum is called rectal cancer. Cancer that affects either of these parts may also be called colorectal cancer.

Another name for Colonic Polyps. Colonic polyps are growths on the inner lining of your colon or rectum. The rectum is the last part of your large intestine. Polyps are common in adults, especially as you get older.
Treatment for colonic diseases varies greatly depending on the disease and its severity. Treatment may involve diet, medicines and in some cases, surgery.
Colonic polyps are growths on the inner lining of your colon or rectum. The rectum is the last part of your large intestine. Polyps are common in adults, especially as you get older.
A test where a doctor uses a thin camera to look inside the large intestine, often to check for colon cancer.
Most of us see our world in color. We enjoy looking at a lush green lawn or a red rose in full bloom. If you have a color vision defect, you may see these colors differently than most people.
Cancer of the colon or rectum. Screening with a colonoscopy or stool test is recommended starting at age 45.

Another name for Colonic Polyps. Colonic polyps are growths on the inner lining of your colon or rectum. The rectum is the last part of your large intestine. Polyps are common in adults, especially as you get older.

A coma is a deep state of unconsciousness. An individual in a coma is alive but unable to move or respond to his or her environment. Coma may occur as a complication of an underlying illness, or as a result of injuries, such as brain injury.
A mild virus infection of the nose and throat, with a runny nose, sneezing and sore throat. Antibiotics do not help a cold.
It is hard when your baby is sick. Common health problems in babies include colds, coughs, fevers, and vomiting. Babies also commonly have skin problems, like diaper rash or cradle cap.

Another name for Infectious Diseases. Germs, or microbes, are found everywhere - in the air, soil, and water. There are also germs on your skin and in your body. Many of them are harmless, and some can even be helpful.

Another name for Speech and Communication Disorders. Some speech and communication problems may be genetic. Often, no one knows the causes. By first grade, about 5% of children have noticeable speech disorders.
A clinic that gives care to everyone, charging less to people with low income or no insurance. Many have interpreters.
A trusted local worker who helps people get health care, understand their care and find resources, often in their own language.
Having more than one health condition at the same time.
Many Americans use medical treatments that are not part of mainstream medicine. When you are using these types of care, it may be called complementary, integrative, or alternative medicine.
Another name for Blood Count Tests. Your blood contains red blood cells (RBC), white blood cells (WBC), and platelets. Blood count tests measure the number and types of cells in your blood.

Complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) is a chronic pain condition. It causes intense pain, usually in the arms, hands, legs, or feet. It may happen after an injury, either to a nerve or to tissue in the affected area.
A new problem that happens because of an illness, treatment or surgery.
A blood test (CMP) that checks blood sugar, salts (electrolytes), kidney function and liver function.

Another name for Herniated Disk. Your backbone, or spine, is made up of 26 bones called vertebrae. In between them are soft disks filled with a jelly-like substance. These disks cushion the vertebrae and keep them in place.
If you have concerns about your gambling, ask for help. Your health care provider can work with you to find the treatment that's best for you.
A brain injury from a blow to the head, which can cause headache, confusion, dizziness or memory problems.

Another name for Child Behavior Disorders. All kids misbehave some times. And some may have temporary behavior problems due to stress. For example, the birth of a sibling, a divorce, or a death in the family may cause a child to act out.

Another name for Genital Warts. Genital warts are a sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by the human papillomavirus (HPV). There are many types of HPV. Some types of HPV can cause genital warts.
Trouble thinking clearly, paying attention or knowing where you are. Sudden confusion needs urgent care.
Present from birth.
A problem with the heart's structure that a baby is born with, such as a hole between chambers.
Congenital heart defects (CHDs) are problems with the structure of the heart. "Congenital" means that that the problems are present at birth.

Another name for Birthmarks. Birthmarks are abnormalities of the skin that are present when a baby is born. There are two types of birthmarks. Vascular birthmarks are made up of blood vessels that haven't formed correctly.
A stuffy, blocked feeling, often in the nose or chest.
Heart failure where fluid builds up in the lungs, legs or belly because the heart cannot pump well enough (CHF).
Pink eye: redness and swelling of the clear layer over the white of the eye, from infection or allergy. Some kinds spread easily.
Your connective tissue supports many different parts of your body, such as your skin, eyes, and heart. It is like a "cellular glue" that gives your body parts their shape and helps keep them strong.
A paper you sign to show you understand and agree to a treatment, test or surgery. You can ask questions before signing.
Having bowel movements less often than usual, or stools that are hard and difficult to pass.
Another name for Eyewear. If you need corrective lenses, you may be able to choose between contacts or glasses. Either usually requires a prescription. Almost anyone can wear glasses.
Able to spread from one person to another.
A small sensor worn on the skin (CGM) that checks blood sugar all day and night and sends readings to a phone or reader.
Birth control: methods used to prevent pregnancy, such as pills, condoms, IUDs or implants.
Tightening of the uterus during labor. Regular contractions that get stronger and closer together mean labor has started.
A reason not to use a certain medicine or treatment because it could be harmful for you.
A liquid given by mouth or into a vein before some scans so that organs and blood vessels show up more clearly. Tell staff if you have kidney problems or allergies.
Another name for Bruises. A bruise is a mark on your skin caused by blood trapped under the surface. It happens when an injury crushes small blood vessels but does not break the skin.

Another name for Thalassemia. Thalassemias are inherited blood disorders. If you have one, your body makes fewer healthy red blood cells and less hemoglobin. Hemoglobin is a protein that carries oxygen to the body.
A fixed amount you pay for a doctor visit or medicine, with your insurance paying the rest.
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a long-term lung disease that makes it hard to breathe, often caused by smoking.
Having a long-term, or chronic, illness can disrupt your life in many ways. You may often be tired and in pain. Your illness might affect your appearance or your physical abilities and independence.
No matter how well you have prepared, you might feel dazed or numb after going through a disaster. You may also feel sad, helpless, or anxious.
Another name for Wilson Disease. Wilson disease is a rare inherited disorder that prevents your body from getting rid of extra copper. You need a small amount of copper from food to stay healthy.
The clear front layer of the eye that covers the colored part and the pupil.
Your cornea is the outermost layer of your eye. It is clear and shaped like a dome. The cornea helps to shield the rest of the eye from germs, dust, and other harmful matter.
Corns and calluses are caused by pressure or friction on your skin. They often appear on feet where the bony parts of your feet rub against your shoes.
Another name for Angioplasty. Angioplasty is a procedure to improve blood flow in coronary arteries that have become narrow or blocked. Your coronary arteries supply oxygen-rich blood to your heart.
The arteries that wrap around the heart and bring blood and oxygen to the heart muscle itself.
Another name for Coronary Artery Disease. Coronary artery disease (CAD) is the most common type of heart disease in the United States and a leading cause of death for both men and women.

Another name for Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery. Coronary artery bypass surgery creates a new path for blood to flow to your heart. This surgery is sometimes called a coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) or heart bypass.
Coronary artery bypass surgery creates a new path for blood to flow to your heart. This surgery is sometimes called a coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) or heart bypass.
Narrowing of the blood vessels that feed the heart, usually from fatty buildup. It can lead to chest pain or a heart attack.

Another name for COVID-19 (Coronavirus Disease 2019). COVID-19 (coronavirus disease 2019) is an illness caused by a virus. This virus is a coronavirus called SARS-CoV-2. It spreads when a person who has the infection breathes out droplets and very small particles that contain the virus.
A strong anti-inflammatory medicine, such as prednisone. It can be a pill, cream, inhaler or shot. Long-term use has side effects.

Another name for Steroids. You may have heard of anabolic steroids, which can have harmful effects. But there's another type of steroid - sometimes called a corticosteroid - that treats a variety of problems.
Cosmetics that treat or prevent diseases are also drugs. Products such as dandruff shampoo, fluoride toothpaste, and antiperspirant deodorant are both cosmetics and drugs.
Forcefully pushing air out of the lungs to clear the airways. A cough lasting more than three weeks should be checked by a doctor.
Talking with a trained professional to work through problems, feelings or stress.
The health services and medicines your insurance plan helps pay for.
An illness caused by the coronavirus SARS-CoV-2. It can cause fever, cough, tiredness and loss of taste or smell, and can be serious for older adults.

COVID-19 (coronavirus disease 2019) is an illness caused by a virus. This virus is a coronavirus called SARS-CoV-2. It spreads when a person who has the infection breathes out droplets and very small particles that contain the virus.
Another name for COVID-19 Testing. Even if your COVID-19 viral test is negative (the test did not detect the virus), you should still take steps to protect yourself and others.
Even if your COVID-19 viral test is negative (the test did not detect the virus), you should still take steps to protect yourself and others.
It's important to stay up to date with the COVID-19 vaccines. Contact your health care provider if you don't know when you need another vaccine or if you have other questions about the vaccines.

Another name for Cerebral Palsy. Cerebral palsy (CP) is a group of neurologic disorders that cause problems with movement, balance, and posture. The first part of the name, cerebral, means having to do with the brain.
Cardiopulmonary resuscitation: pressing hard and fast on the chest (and sometimes giving breaths) to keep blood flowing when someone's heart has stopped.

Another name for Pubic Lice. Pubic lice (also called crabs) are tiny insects which usually live in the pubic or genital area of humans. They are also sometimes found on other coarse body hair, such as hair on the legs, armpits, mustache, beard, eyebrows, or eyelashes.

Another name for Cocaine. Cocaine is a very addictive drug that is made from leaves of the coca plant found in South America. It is mostly available as an illegal drug that some people use to get high.
A sudden, painful tightening of a muscle that you cannot control.

Another name for Head Injuries. Chances are you've bumped your head before. Often, the injury is minor because your skull is hard and it protects your brain. But other head injuries can be more severe, such as a skull fracture, concussion, or traumatic brain injury.
Craniofacial is a medical term that relates to the bones of the skull and face. Craniofacial abnormalities are birth defects of the face or head.
A waste product in the blood that the kidneys remove. A high level can mean the kidneys are not working well.

Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) is a rare, degenerative brain disorder. Symptoms usually start around age 60. Memory problems, behavior changes, vision problems, and poor muscle coordination progress quickly to dementia, coma, and death.

Another name for Sudden Infant Death Syndrome. Sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS) is the sudden, unexplained death of an infant younger than one year old. Some people call SIDS "crib death" because many babies who die of SIDS are found in their cribs.
Critical care is medical care for people who have life-threatening injuries and illnesses. It usually takes place in an intensive care unit (ICU).
A long-term disease that causes inflammation in the digestive tract, with belly pain, diarrhea and weight loss.
Croup is an inflammation of the vocal cords (larynx) and windpipe (trachea). It causes difficulty breathing, a barking cough, and a hoarse voice.
C-reactive protein: a blood test that shows inflammation in the body.

Another name for Complex Regional Pain Syndrome. Complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) is a chronic pain condition. It causes intense pain, usually in the arms, hands, legs, or feet. It may happen after an injury, either to a nerve or to tissue in the affected area.

Another name for Cryptosporidiosis. Cryptosporidiosis is a contagious disease that causes watery diarrhea. It is caused by parasites called Cryptosporidium, or Crypto . These parasites live in soil, food, and water.
Cryptosporidiosis is a contagious disease that causes watery diarrhea. It is caused by parasites called Cryptosporidium, or Crypto . These parasites live in soil, food, and water.
Another name for Methamphetamine. Methamphetamine - meth for short - is a very addictive stimulant drug. It is a powder that can be made into a pill or a shiny rock (called a crystal).

Another name for Cat Scratch Disease. For people with weak immune systems, CSD may cause more serious problems. The best way to avoid CSD is to avoid rough play with cats that could lead to scratches or bites.
A test that uses X-rays and a computer to make detailed pictures of the inside of the body.
Computed tomography (CT) is a type of medical imaging test that uses special x-ray equipment to make detailed pictures of the inside of your body.

Cushing syndrome is a hormonal disorder. It happens when your body has too much of a hormone called cortisol over a long period of time. Hormones are chemical messengers in your bloodstream that control the actions of certain cells or organs.
Another name for Skin Conditions. NIH: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases

Another name for Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome. Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS) is a group of inherited disorders that weaken connective tissues. Connective tissues are proteins that support skin, bones, blood vessels, and other organs.

Another name for Stroke. A stroke happens when there is a loss of blood flow to part of the brain. Your brain cells cannot get the oxygen and nutrients they need from blood, and they start to die within a few minutes.

Physical activity that makes your body work, such as walking, swimming or biking. Adults should aim for about 150 minutes a week.

Even if your eyes feel healthy, you could have a problem and not know it. That's why regular eye exams are so important. Refractive errors are the most common type of vision problem that makes it hard to see clearly.
A check of your vision and eye health. A dilated eye exam uses drops to widen the pupils so the doctor can see the back of the eye.

The structure of your face helps protect your eyes from injury. Still, injuries can damage your eye, sometimes severely enough that you could lose your vision.

Feeling very tired or low on energy, even after rest.

Another name for Bowel Movement. A bowel movement is the last stop in the movement of food through your digestive tract. Your stool passes out of your body through the rectum and anus.
A tube that carries liquid food directly into the stomach or intestine for people who cannot eat safely by mouth.

A long-term condition with pain all over the body, tiredness, and trouble with sleep and memory.

Illness from eating food or drink with germs or toxins in it, causing vomiting, diarrhea and stomach cramps.

Baby milk made from cow's milk or soy, used instead of or along with breast milk.

Damage to skin and tissue from freezing, most often on fingers, toes, nose and ears.

Stomach flu: an infection of the stomach and intestines with vomiting and diarrhea. It is not the same as influenza.

Medicine that puts you into a deep, sleep-like state during surgery so you feel nothing.
A medicine with the same active ingredient as a brand-name drug, usually much cheaper.
Genes are sections of DNA in your cells that are passed down (inherited) from your parents. You inherit two copies of each gene, one from each parent.
A genetic brain disorder is caused by a variation or a mutation in a gene. A variation is a different form of a gene. A mutation is a change in a gene.
Genetic counseling provides information and support to people who have, or may be at risk for, genetic disorders. A genetic counselor meets with you to discuss genetic risks.

Guillain-Barre syndrome is a rare disorder that causes your immune system to attack your peripheral nervous system (PNS). The PNS nerves connect your brain and spinal cord with the rest of your body.

Another name for Polycystic Ovary Syndrome. Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), also known as polyendocrine metabolic ovary syndrome (PMOS), is the name of a hormonal disorder. PCOS affects the ovaries, as well as many other parts of the body.

Another name for Asthma in Children. Asthma is a chronic (long-term) lung disease. It affects your airways, the tubes that carry air in and out of your lungs. When you have asthma, your airways can become inflamed and narrowed.
Another name for Reflux in Infants. Gastroesophageal reflux (GER), often called reflux or spitting up, happens when food or milk comes back up from your baby's stomach into the esophagus.
A doctor who specializes in caring for babies, children and teenagers.

Another name for Head Lice. Head lice are tiny insects that live on people's heads. Adult lice are about the size of sesame seeds. The eggs, called nits, are even smaller - about the size of a dandruff flake.

The pelvic floor is a group of muscles and other tissues that form a sling or hammock across the pelvis. In women, it holds the uterus, bladder, bowel, and other pelvic organs in place so that they can work properly.
Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) is an infection of the uterus, ovaries, and other female reproductive organs. PID causes scarring in these organs.
Pelvic pain occurs mostly in the lower abdomen area. The pain might be steady, or it might come and go. It can be a sharp and stabbing pain in a specific spot, or a dull pain that is spread out.

Another name for Pelvic Floor Disorders. The pelvic floor is a group of muscles and other tissues that form a sling or hammock across the pelvis. In women, it holds the uterus, bladder, bowel, and other pelvic organs in place so that they can work properly.
The ring of bones at the base of the spine that connects to the legs; also the lower part of the belly.
Pemphigus is an autoimmune disorder. If you have it, your immune system attacks healthy cells in your skin and mouth, causing blisters and sores.
One of the first and most common antibiotics. Some people are allergic to it.
A sore in the lining of the stomach or the first part of the small intestine. It can cause burning stomach pain.
Another name for Angioplasty. Angioplasty is a procedure to improve blood flow in coronary arteries that have become narrow or blocked. Your coronary arteries supply oxygen-rich blood to your heart.
Symptoms of pericardial problems include chest pain, rapid heartbeat, and difficulty breathing. Fever is a common symptom of acute pericarditis.
Inflammation of the thin sac around the heart. It often causes sharp chest pain that gets worse when lying down or breathing in.

Another name for Menstruation. Menstruation, also called a period, is normal vaginal bleeding that happens as part of the monthly cycle in women and girls. Every month, the body prepares for pregnancy.
Menstruation, or period, is normal vaginal bleeding that happens as part of a woman's monthly cycle. Many women have painful periods, also called dysmenorrhea.

Another name for Gum Disease. If you have gum disease, you're not alone. Many U.S. adults currently have some form of the disease. It ranges from simple gum inflammation, called gingivitis, to serious damage to the tissue and bone supporting the teeth.
Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) happens when there is a narrowing of the blood vessels outside of your heart. The cause of PAD is atherosclerosis.
Narrowed arteries in the legs or arms (PAD), usually from plaque buildup. It can cause leg pain when walking.

Nerves are like wires that carry messages back and forth between your brain and your body. Your peripheral nerves branch off from your brain and spinal cord and connect to all parts of your body, including your muscles and organs.

Another name for Peripheral Nerve Disorders. Nerves are like wires that carry messages back and forth between your brain and your body. Your peripheral nerves branch off from your brain and spinal cord and connect to all parts of your body, including your muscles and organs.

Another name for Peripheral Nerve Disorders. Nerves are like wires that carry messages back and forth between your brain and your body. Your peripheral nerves branch off from your brain and spinal cord and connect to all parts of your body, including your muscles and organs.
Your peritoneum is the tissue that lines your abdominal wall and covers most of the organs in your abdomen. A liquid, peritoneal fluid, lubricates the surface of this tissue.

Another name for Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease. Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT) is a group of genetic nerve disorders. It is named after the three doctors who first identified it. In the United States, CMT affects about 1 in 2,500 people.
You've probably seen your chart at your doctor's office. In fact, you may have charts at several doctors' offices. If you've been in the hospital, you have a chart there, too.

Another name for E-Cigarettes. E-cigarettes, or electronic cigarettes, are battery-operated smoking devices. They often look like cigarettes, but work differently. Using an e-cigarette is called vaping.
Your personality is your own way of thinking, feeling, behaving, and relating to others. Once you become an adult, your personality usually doesn't change much.
Another name for Sweat. Sweat is a clear, salty liquid produced by glands in your skin. Sweating is how your body cools itself. You sweat mainly under your arms and on your feet and palms.
Another name for Whooping Cough. Whooping cough, or pertussis, is a respiratory infection that can cause coughing fits. In serious cases, the coughing can become violent and rapid.
Another name for Autism Spectrum Disorder. Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurological and developmental disorder that begins early in childhood and lasts throughout a person's life.
Pests live where they are not wanted or cause harm to crops, people, or animals. Pesticides can help get rid of them. Pesticides are not just insect killers.
A scan that uses a small amount of a radioactive tracer to show how organs and tissues are working. It is often used to look for cancer.
A trained expert who prepares and gives out medicine and can answer questions about how to take it.
A store or counter where prescription and other medicines are sold.

Another name for Throat Cancer. Throat cancer is a type of head and neck cancer. Throat cancer has different names, depending on which part of the throat is affected. The different parts of your throat are called the oropharynx, the hypopharynx, the nasopharynx, and the larynx, or voice box.
Another name for Throat Disorders. Your throat is a tube that carries food to your esophagus and air to your windpipe and larynx. The technical name for your throat is the pharynx.
Another name for Sore Throat. Your throat is a tube that carries food to your esophagus and air to your windpipe and larynx (also called the voice box). The technical name for the throat is pharynx.
Phenylketonuria (PKU) is a type of amino acid metabolism disorder. It is inherited. If you have it, your body can't process phenylalanine (Phe).
Sometimes pheochromocytoma is part of another condition called multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome (MEN). People with MEN often have other cancers and other problems involving hormones.
A trained worker who takes blood samples.
A phobia is a type of anxiety disorder. It is a strong, irrational fear of something that poses little or no real danger.
When a doctor or nurse checks your body by looking, listening, and feeling, such as listening to your heart and lungs.
A licensed professional who helps people move better and recover strength after injury, surgery or illness.
Treatment with exercise and hands-on care to help you move better and recover from injury or surgery.
A licensed health professional (PA) who examines, diagnoses and treats patients, working with doctors.
Another name for Herbal Medicine. An herb is a plant or plant part used for its scent, flavor, or therapeutic properties. Herbal medicines are one type of dietary supplement.
Another name for Pelvic Inflammatory Disease. Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) is an infection of the uterus, ovaries, and other female reproductive organs. PID causes scarring in these organs.
Piercings and tattoos are body decorations that go back to ancient times. Body piercing involves making a hole in the skin so that you can insert jewelry.
Another name for Hemorrhoids. Too much straining, rubbing, or cleaning around your anus may make your symptoms worse. For many people, the symptoms of external hemorrhoids go away within a few days.
A box with sections for each day (and time of day) to help you take medicines on schedule.
Another name for Acne. Acne is a common skin disease that causes pimples. Pimples form when hair follicles under your skin clog up. Most pimples form on the face, neck, back, chest, and shoulders.

Pink eye usually does not affect vision. Infectious pink eye can easily spread from one person to another. The infection will clear in most cases without medical care, but bacterial pink eye needs treatment with antibiotic eye drops or ointment.
Pinworms are small parasites that can live in the colon and rectum. You get them when you swallow their eggs. The eggs hatch inside your intestines.

Another name for Smoking. There's no way around it; smoking is bad for your health. It harms nearly every organ of the body, even some that you would not expect. Cigarette smoking causes many cancers and other health problems.
Your pituitary gland is a pea-sized gland at the base of your brain. The pituitary is the "master control gland" - it makes hormones that affect growth and the functions of other glands in the body.
A pea-sized gland at the base of the brain that controls many other glands and hormones.

Another name for Phenylketonuria. Phenylketonuria (PKU) is a type of amino acid metabolism disorder. It is inherited. If you have it, your body can't process phenylalanine (Phe).

Plague is an infection caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. The bacteria are found mainly in rats and in the fleas that feed on them. People and other animals can get plague from rat or flea bites.
Heel pain caused by an irritated band of tissue on the bottom of the foot. It is often worst with the first steps in the morning.
A fatty, waxy buildup inside an artery wall that narrows it. In the mouth, plaque is a sticky film of germs on the teeth.
The yellowish liquid part of the blood that carries blood cells, nutrients and hormones.

Another name for Multiple Myeloma. Multiple myeloma is a cancer that begins in plasma cells, a type of white blood cell. These cells are part of your immune system, which helps protect the body from germs and other harmful substances.

Tiny pieces in the blood that clump together to stop bleeding.
Your pleura is a large, thin sheet of tissue that wraps around the outside of your lungs and lines the inside of your chest cavity. Between the layers of the pleura is a very thin space.

Another name for Lead Poisoning. Breathing air, drinking water, eating food, or swallowing or touching dirt that contains lead can cause many health problems. Lead can affect almost every organ and system in your body.

Another name for Premenstrual Syndrome. Premenstrual syndrome, or PMS, is a group of physical and emotional symptoms that start one to two weeks before your period. Most women have at least some symptoms of PMS, and the symptoms go away after their periods start.
How the diagnosis is made depends upon where the infection is. Your doctor will do a physical exam and ask about your medical history. Possible tests may include blood, imaging, or lab tests.
Pneumocystis jirovecii can spread from person to person through the air. You can spread it to others even if it isn't making you sick.
An infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, causing cough, fever and trouble breathing.
A vaccine that protects against pneumococcal bacteria, a common cause of pneumonia. It is recommended for adults 50 and older and some younger people.

Another name for Plague. Plague is an infection caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. The bacteria are found mainly in rats and in the fleas that feed on them. People and other animals can get plague from rat or flea bites.
On a prescription, means 'by mouth': swallow the medicine.
A doctor who treats feet and ankles. People with diabetes often see one for foot checks.
Another name for Primary Ovarian Insufficiency. Primary ovarian insufficiency (POI) happens when your ovaries stop working normally before you are 40.
Another name for Primary Ovarian Insufficiency. Primary ovarian insufficiency (POI) happens when your ovaries stop working normally before you are 40.
A free, 24-hour helpline for poisonings and medicine mistakes. In the U.S., call 1-800-222-1222.
If you spend time outdoors, chances are you have been bothered by poison ivy, poison oak or poison sumac at some point. Most people are sensitive to the plants' oily sap.
Harm from swallowing, breathing in or touching something toxic. Call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 or 911.
Polio, or poliomyelitis, is a disease that spreads from person to person. It is caused by the poliovirus. The virus attacks the nervous system.
Another name for Polio and Post-Polio Syndrome. Polio, or poliomyelitis, is a disease that spreads from person to person. It is caused by the poliovirus. The virus attacks the nervous system.
Another name for Hay Fever. Each spring, summer, and fall, trees, weeds, and grasses release tiny pollen grains into the air. Some of the pollen ends up in your nose and throat.
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), also known as polyendocrine metabolic ovary syndrome (PMOS), is the name of a hormonal disorder. PCOS affects the ovaries, as well as many other parts of the body.
Polymyalgia rheumatica is a disorder that causes muscle pain and stiffness in your neck, shoulders, and hips. It is most common in women and almost always occurs in people over 50.
A small growth on the inside lining of an organ, such as the colon or nose. Most are not cancer, but some colon polyps can turn into cancer, so they are removed.

Another name for Dietary Fats. Fat is a type of nutrient. You need some fat in your diet but not too much. Fats give you energy and help your body absorb vitamins. Dietary fat also plays a major role in your cholesterol levels.
Another name for Bowel Movement. A bowel movement is the last stop in the movement of food through your digestive tract. Your stool passes out of your body through the rectum and anus.

Porphyrias are a group of genetic disorders caused by problems with how your body makes a substance called heme. Heme is found throughout the body, especially in your blood and bone marrow, where it carries oxygen.
A small device placed under the skin of the chest so medicines (such as chemotherapy) can be given and blood drawn without a new needle in the arm each time.
A test result that found what was being tested for. For many tests this means you have the condition.
Another name for Long COVID. There are several other names for long COVID. It can also be called post-COVID conditions, long-haul COVID, and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC).
Another name for Long COVID. There are several other names for long COVID. It can also be called post-COVID conditions, long-haul COVID, and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC).

Another name for HIV: PrEP and PEP. If you have a partner who is HIV-positive and are considering getting pregnant, talk to your health care provider about PrEP. Taking it may help protect you and your fetus or baby from getting an HIV infection while you try to get pregnant, during pregnancy, or while breastfeeding.
After surgery. Post-op care includes pain control, wound care and follow-up visits.

Another name for Postpartum Depression. Having a baby can be exciting, but it can also be stressful and bring many strong emotions. During the postpartum period, which is the time after you give birth, you may have mood swings, crying spells, or feel anxious.

Another name for Postpartum Care. In addition to physical changes, you may feel sad or have the "baby blues." If you are extremely sad or are unable to care for yourself or your baby, you might have a serious condition called postpartum depression.

Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a mental health disorder that some people develop after they experience or see a traumatic event. The traumatic event may be life-threatening, such as combat, a natural disaster, a car accident, or sexual assault.

Another name for After Surgery. After any operation, you'll have some side effects. There is usually some pain with surgery. There may also be swelling and soreness around the area that the surgeon cut.
The weeks and months after giving birth.

In addition to physical changes, you may feel sad or have the "baby blues." If you are extremely sad or are unable to care for yourself or your baby, you might have a serious condition called postpartum depression.
Depression after having a baby that is stronger and lasts longer than the 'baby blues'. It is common and treatable.

Another name for Cannabis. Cannabis, also known as marijuana, is a green, brown, or gray mixture of dried parts from the cannabis plant. The plant contains chemicals that affect the brain and can change how you feel or think.
A mineral that helps nerves, muscles and the heart work. Levels that are too high or too low can cause dangerous heart rhythms.
Preferred provider organization: an insurance plan that lets you see doctors in or out of its network, usually without a referral, but costs less in-network.
Another name for Polio and Post-Polio Syndrome. Polio, or poliomyelitis, is a disease that spreads from person to person. It is caused by the poliovirus. The virus attacks the nervous system.
Prader-Willi Syndrome (PWS) is a rare genetic disorder. It causes poor muscle tone, low levels of sex hormones and a constant feeling of hunger.

Another name for HIV: PrEP and PEP. If you have a partner who is HIV-positive and are considering getting pregnant, talk to your health care provider about PrEP. Taking it may help protect you and your fetus or baby from getting an HIV infection while you try to get pregnant, during pregnancy, or while breastfeeding.
Before surgery. Pre-op instructions may tell you when to stop eating and which medicines to stop.

If you are trying to have a baby or are just thinking about it, it is not too early to prepare for a safe pregnancy and a healthy baby. You should see your health care provider for preconception care.
Blood sugar that is higher than normal but not yet high enough to be diabetes. Healthy eating and exercise can stop it from turning into diabetes.
A corticosteroid pill used to calm inflammation in many conditions. Do not stop it suddenly if you have taken it for a while.
A serious condition in pregnancy with high blood pressure and signs of organ damage. Warning signs include bad headaches, vision changes and sudden swelling.
Another name for Premature Babies. Almost 1 of every 10 infants born in the United States are premature, or preemies. A premature birth is when a baby is born before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy.
A health problem you had before your health insurance started. Under U.S. law, most plans cannot refuse you or charge more because of it.
Your body will keep changing as your fetus develops until your baby is ready to be born. It can be hard to know whether a new symptom is normal or could be a sign of a problem.
Always talk to your provider before you stop or start any medicine. You may take medicine to treat a health problem you had before pregnancy.
Nutrition is about eating a healthy and balanced diet so your body gets the nutrients that it needs. Nutrients are substances in foods that our bodies need so they can function and grow.
You may need to take medicines while you are pregnant. But not all medicines are safe during pregnancy. Many medicines carry risks for you, your baby, or both.
During pregnancy, there are many things you can do to keep yourself and your baby healthy. They include getting regular prenatal care, eating healthy, and staying active.
A urine or blood test that checks for a hormone made during pregnancy.
Almost 1 of every 10 infants born in the United States are premature, or preemies. A premature birth is when a baby is born before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy.
When a baby is born before 37 weeks of pregnancy. Premature babies may need extra care.
Another name for Preterm Labor. Preterm labor is labor that starts before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy. It can lead to premature birth. Premature babies may face serious health risks.
Another name for Primary Ovarian Insufficiency. Primary ovarian insufficiency (POI) happens when your ovaries stop working normally before you are 40.

Premenstrual syndrome, or PMS, is a group of physical and emotional symptoms that start one to two weeks before your period. Most women have at least some symptoms of PMS, and the symptoms go away after their periods start.
The amount you pay every month for health insurance.
Checkups and care during pregnancy to keep mother and baby healthy.
Prenatal testing provides information about the health of your fetus before the baby is born. Some routine tests during pregnancy also check your health.
Vitamins made for pregnancy, with extra folic acid and iron.

Another name for Hearing Disorders and Deafness. It's frustrating to be unable to hear well enough to enjoy talking with friends or family. Hearing disorders make it hard, but not impossible, to hear.
A doctor's written order for a medicine or treatment.
A program, often from a drug company or nonprofit, that gives free or low-cost medicine to people who qualify.

Another name for Prescription Drug Misuse. Misusing some prescription drugs can lead to addiction. These include opioids, sedatives, tranquilizers, and stimulants. Drug addiction is a chronic brain disease.
Misusing some prescription drugs can lead to addiction. These include opioids, sedatives, tranquilizers, and stimulants. Drug addiction is a chronic brain disease.
The sticker on your medicine bottle showing your name, the medicine, the dose, how often to take it and refills left. Ask the pharmacist to explain anything unclear.
Pressure sores are areas of damaged skin caused by staying in one position for too long. They commonly form where your bones are close to your skin, such as your ankles, back, elbows, heels and hips.
A bedsore: an injury to skin and tissue from lying or sitting in one position too long.

Another name for Pressure Sores. Pressure sores are areas of damaged skin caused by staying in one position for too long. They commonly form where your bones are close to your skin, such as your ankles, back, elbows, heels and hips.
Another name for Preterm Labor. Preterm labor is labor that starts before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy. It can lead to premature birth. Premature babies may face serious health risks.
Preterm labor is labor that starts before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy. It can lead to premature birth. Premature babies may face serious health risks.
Care that helps prevent illness or find it early, such as checkups, vaccines and screenings. Many plans cover it at no cost.

Another name for Addison Disease. Your adrenal glands are just above your kidneys. The outside layer of these glands makes hormones that help your body respond to stress and regulate your blood pressure and water and salt balance.
PCP: your main doctor for checkups and everyday health problems, who refers you to specialists when needed.
Primary ovarian insufficiency (POI) happens when your ovaries stop working normally before you are 40.
Approval you must get from your insurance before certain treatments, tests or medicines, or it may not pay.

Another name for Laser Eye Surgery. For many people, laser eye surgery can correct their vision so they no longer need glasses or contact lenses. Laser eye surgery reshapes the cornea, the clear front part of the eye.
On a prescription, means 'as needed': take the medicine only when you need it, such as for pain, not on a schedule.
Live 'good' bacteria in some foods and supplements that may help digestion.
The likely course or outcome of an illness.
Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is a rare brain disease. It happens because of damage to nerve cells in the brain. PSP affects your movement, including control of your walking and balance.

Another name for Herniated Disk. Your backbone, or spine, is made up of 26 bones called vertebrae. In between them are soft disks filled with a jelly-like substance. These disks cushion the vertebrae and keep them in place.
Treatment given to prevent a disease, such as a vaccine or medicine before a trip.
A walnut-sized gland in men, below the bladder, that makes part of the fluid in semen. It often grows larger with age.
Cancer of the prostate gland in men. It is common and often grows slowly.
Cancer is a disease when the cells of the body grow out of control. Cancer screening is having tests to look for signs of cancer before you have any symptoms.
The prostate is a gland in the male reproductive system. It lies just below the bladder. It makes fluid that is part of semen.
A nutrient in foods like meat, fish, eggs, beans and nuts that builds and repairs muscles and tissues.
Closer to the center of the body. The elbow is proximal to the wrist.

Another name for Itching. Itching is an irritating sensation that makes you want to scratch your skin. Sometimes it can feel like pain, but it is different. Often, you feel itchy in one area in your body, but sometimes you may feel itching all over.
A blood test for prostate-specific antigen, which can be higher with prostate cancer or an enlarged prostate.

Another name for C. diff Infections. C. diff is a bacterium that can cause diarrhea and more serious intestinal conditions such as colitis. You may see it called other names, such as Clostridioides difficile (the new name), Clostridium difficile (an older name), and C. difficile.
A skin condition that causes thick, red, scaly patches, often on the elbows, knees and scalp.

Psoriasis is a skin disease that causes itchy or sore patches of thick, red skin with silvery scales. You usually get them on your elbows, knees, scalp, back, face, palms and feet, but they can show up on other parts of your body.

Another name for Progressive Supranuclear Palsy. Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is a rare brain disease. It happens because of damage to nerve cells in the brain. PSP affects your movement, including control of your walking and balance.
A medical doctor who treats mental health conditions and can prescribe medicine.

Another name for Stress. Stress is how your brain and body respond to a challenge or demand. When you are stressed, your body releases certain hormones. Hormones are chemicals that travel in your bloodstream and control how different parts of your body work.
A mental health professional who provides therapy and testing but usually does not prescribe medicine.
Another name for Psychotic Disorders. Psychotic disorders are severe mental disorders that cause abnormal thinking and perceptions. People with psychoses lose touch with reality.
Talk therapy: treatment for mental health problems by talking with a trained professional.
Psychotic disorders are severe mental disorders that cause abnormal thinking and perceptions. People with psychoses lose touch with reality.
Another name for Folic Acid. Folic acid is a B vitamin. It helps the body make healthy new cells. Everyone needs folic acid. For women who may get pregnant, it is really important.
Post-traumatic stress disorder: a mental health condition after a frightening or dangerous event, with nightmares, flashbacks and strong anxiety.
Puberty is the time in life when a boy or girl becomes sexually mature. It is a process that usually happens between ages 8 and 13 for girls and ages 9 and 14 for boys.

Pubic lice (also called crabs) are tiny insects which usually live in the pubic or genital area of humans. They are also sometimes found on other coarse body hair, such as hair on the legs, armpits, mustache, beard, eyebrows, or eyelashes.

Another name for Pulmonary Hypertension. Pulmonary hypertension, sometimes called PH, is a serious condition that affects the blood vessels in the lungs. It develops when the blood pressure in your lungs is higher than normal.
A blood clot that has traveled to the lungs (PE). It causes sudden shortness of breath and chest pain and is an emergency.
Another name for Emphysema. Emphysema is a type of COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). COPD is a group of lung diseases that make it hard to breathe and get worse over time.

Pulmonary fibrosis is a condition in which the tissue deep in your lungs becomes scarred over time. This tissue gets thick and stiff. That makes it hard for you to catch your breath, and your blood may not get enough oxygen.
Pulmonary hypertension, sometimes called PH, is a serious condition that affects the blood vessels in the lungs. It develops when the blood pressure in your lungs is higher than normal.
Pulmonary rehabilitation, also known as pulmonary rehab or PR, is a program for people who have chronic (ongoing) breathing problems. It can help improve your ability to function and quality of life.
A doctor who treats lung and breathing problems.
Your heartbeat, felt in the wrist or neck. A normal adult resting pulse is about 60 to 100 beats a minute.
A small clip put on a finger that measures your pulse and the oxygen level in your blood.
A deep, narrow wound from something sharp like a nail. It may need a tetanus shot.
Another name for Prader-Willi Syndrome. Prader-Willi Syndrome (PWS) is a rare genetic disorder. It causes poor muscle tone, low levels of sex hormones and a constant feeling of hunger.
Another name for Fever. A fever is a body temperature that is higher than normal. A normal temperature can vary from person to person, but it is usually around 98.6 °F (37 °C).

Another name for Heartburn. Heartburn is a painful burning feeling in your chest or throat. It happens when stomach acid backs up into your esophagus, the tube that carries food from your mouth to your stomach.
On a prescription, means once a day. Many prescriptions now just say 'daily'.
Another name for Health Fraud. Health fraud scams involve selling medicines, supplements, devices, foods, or cosmetics that have not been proven effective. At best, these scams don't work.
Another name for Paralysis. Paralysis is the loss of muscle function in part of your body. It happens when something goes wrong with the way messages pass between your brain and muscles.
Keeping people who may have been exposed to a contagious disease apart from others to see if they get sick.
Quitting smoking is important for your health. Besides being the leading cause of cancer in the United States, smoking tobacco harms most organs of your body and causes many other health problems.

Another name for Rheumatoid Arthritis. Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a form of arthritis that causes pain, swelling, and stiffness in your joints. RA is an autoimmune disease. Although it is most common in the wrist and fingers, this disease can cause your immune system to attack any joint tissue.
Rabies is a deadly animal disease caused by a virus. It can happen in wild animals, including raccoons, skunks, bats and foxes, or in dogs, cats or farm animals.
Another name for Rickets. Rickets causes soft, weak bones in children. It usually occurs when they do not get enough vitamin D, which helps growing bones absorb the minerals calcium and phosphorous.
A lot of radiation over a short period can cause burns or radiation sickness. If the exposure is large enough, it can cause premature aging or even death.
Background radiation is all around us all the time. Most of it forms naturally from minerals. These radioactive minerals are in the ground, soil, water, and even our bodies.
Cancer treatment that uses high-energy beams, like strong X-rays, to kill cancer cells.
Another name for X-Rays. X-rays are a painless medical imaging test. They send a small amount of radiation through your body to create pictures of bones and organs.

Another name for Nuclear Scans. A nuclear scan is a type of medical imaging test that uses a small amount of radioactive material, called a radiotracer. This scan shows how organs and tissues are working, not just what they look like.
The medical field that uses X-rays, scans and other imaging to see inside the body.

Another name for Nuclear Scans. A nuclear scan is a type of medical imaging test that uses a small amount of radioactive material, called a radiotracer. This scan shows how organs and tissues are working, not just what they look like.

Another name for Radiation Therapy. Radiation therapy is a cancer treatment. It uses high doses of radiation to kill cancer cells and stop them from spreading. It may also be used for easing cancer symptoms.
Radon is a naturally occurring radioactive gas. It is invisible and has no odor or taste. It comes from the normal decay of uranium and thorium.

Another name for Sexual Assault. Sexual assault is any kind of sexual activity, contact, or experience that happens without your consent. That means the sexual activity happens even though you don't agree to it.
A rare disease is one that affects fewer than 200,000 people in the United States. There are nearly 7,000 rare diseases. More than 25 million Americans have one.
A change in the skin's color or texture, such as red spots, bumps or blisters.
A rash is an area of irritated or swollen skin. Many rashes are itchy, red, painful, and irritated. Some rashes can also lead to blisters or patches of raw skin.
Raynaud phenomenon is a condition that affects your blood vessels (the tubes that your blood flows through). It causes your blood vessels to narrow, which decreases blood flow.

Another name for Raynaud Phenomenon. Raynaud phenomenon is a condition that affects your blood vessels (the tubes that your blood flows through). It causes your blood vessels to narrow, which decreases blood flow.
