Another name for Neurofibromatosis. Neurofibromatosis is a genetic disorder of the nervous system. It mainly affects how nerve cells form and grow. It causes tumors to grow on nerves.

Another name for After Surgery. After any operation, you'll have some side effects. There is usually some pain with surgery. There may also be swelling and soreness around the area that the surgeon cut.
The area where patients are watched closely as they wake up after surgery.

Another name for Colorectal Cancer. Cancer that begins in the colon is called colon cancer, and cancer that begins in the rectum is called rectal cancer. Cancer that affects either of these parts may also be called colorectal cancer.
The rectum is the lower part of your large intestine where your body stores stool. Problems with the rectum are common. They include hemorrhoids, abscesses, incontinence and cancer.

Another name for Pelvic Floor Disorders. The pelvic floor is a group of muscles and other tissues that form a sling or hammock across the pelvis. In women, it holds the uterus, bladder, bowel, and other pelvic organs in place so that they can work properly.
The last part of the large intestine, just before the anus, where stool is held.
Blood cells that carry oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body. They contain hemoglobin.

Another name for Cannabis. Cannabis, also known as marijuana, is a green, brown, or gray mixture of dried parts from the cannabis plant. The plant contains chemicals that affect the brain and can change how you feel or think.
A note from your doctor sending you to see a specialist. Some insurance plans require one.
Getting more of a prescription medicine. Your prescription label shows how many refills are left.

Another name for Complex Regional Pain Syndrome. Complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) is a chronic pain condition. It causes intense pain, usually in the arms, hands, legs, or feet. It may happen after an injury, either to a nerve or to tissue in the affected area.
Gastroesophageal reflux (GER), often called reflux, occurs when food or stomach acid flows back from your child's stomach into the esophagus.
Gastroesophageal reflux (GER), often called reflux or spitting up, happens when food or milk comes back up from your baby's stomach into the esophagus.
The cornea and lens of your eye bend (refract) light rays to focus them on the retina. Refractive errors happen when the shape of your eye prevents light from focusing correctly on the retina.

Another name for Crohn's Disease. Crohn's disease is a chronic (long-lasting) disease that causes inflammation in your digestive tract. It can affect any part of your digestive tract, which runs from your mouth to your anus.

Another name for Crohn's Disease. Crohn's disease is a chronic (long-lasting) disease that causes inflammation in your digestive tract. It can affect any part of your digestive tract, which runs from your mouth to your anus.

Another name for Rehabilitation. Rehabilitation is care that can help you get back, keep, or improve abilities that you need for daily life. These abilities may be physical, mental, and/or cognitive (thinking and learning).
Treatment that helps you regain skills and strength after an illness, injury or surgery.
When a disease comes back or gets worse after improving.
When signs of a disease, like cancer, lessen or go away.

Another name for Kidney Cancer. You have two kidneys. They are fist-sized organs on either side of your backbone above your waist. The tubes inside filter and clean your blood, taking out waste products and making urine.

Another name for Dialysis. When your kidneys are healthy, they clean your blood. They also make hormones that keep your bones strong and your blood healthy. When your kidneys fail, you need treatment to replace the work your kidneys used to do.

Another name for Kidney Diseases. You have two kidneys, each about the size of your fist. They are near the middle of your back, just below the rib cage. Inside each kidney there are about a million tiny structures called nephrons.
Another name for Kidney Failure. Healthy kidneys clean your blood by removing excess fluid, minerals, and wastes. They also make hormones that keep your bones strong and your blood healthy.

Another name for Kidney Tests. You have two kidneys. They are fist-sized organs on either side of your backbone above your waist. Your kidneys filter and clean your blood, taking out waste products and making urine.

Another name for Kidney Transplantation. A kidney transplant is an operation that places a healthy kidney in your body. The transplanted kidney takes over the work of the two kidneys that failed, so you no longer need dialysis.
You may be exposed to reproductive hazards through contact with your skin, breathing them in, or swallowing them. This can happen anywhere, but it is more common in the workplace or at home.

Another name for Assisted Living. Assisted living is housing and services for people who need some help with daily care. They may need help with things like dressing, bathing, taking their medicines, and cleaning.
Having to do with breathing and the lungs.
Respiratory failure is a condition in which your blood doesn't have enough oxygen or has too much carbon dioxide. Sometimes you can have both problems.
How many breaths you take in one minute. A normal adult rate at rest is about 12 to 20.

Respiratory syncytial virus, or RSV, is a common respiratory virus. It usually causes mild, cold-like symptoms. But it can cause serious lung infections, especially in infants, older adults, and people with serious medical problems.

Restless legs syndrome (RLS) causes a powerful urge to move your legs. Your legs become uncomfortable when you are lying down or sitting. Some people describe it as a creeping, crawling, tingling, or burning sensation.
Another name for Cardiomyopathy. Cardiomyopathy is the name for diseases of the heart muscle. These diseases enlarge your heart muscle or make it thicker and more rigid than normal.
The thin layer at the back of the eye that senses light and sends pictures to the brain.
Symptoms include an increase in the number of floaters, which are little "cobwebs" or specks that float about in your field of vision, and/or light flashes in the eye.
Retinal disorders are conditions that affect the retina, the thin light-sensitive tissue at the back of your eye. The retina senses light and sends signals to your brain so you can see.
Rett syndrome has no cure. You can treat some of the symptoms with medicines, surgery, and physical and speech therapy. Most people with Rett syndrome live into middle age and beyond.
If these symptoms occur soon after a viral illness, seek medical attention immediately. Reye syndrome can lead to a coma and brain death, so quick diagnosis and treatment are critical.
There are four major blood types: A, B, O, and AB. The types are based on substances found on your blood cells. Your blood type also has a positive or negative sign.
An illness that can follow untreated strep throat and can damage the heart valves for life.
An autoimmune disease where the immune system attacks the joints, causing pain, swelling and stiffness, often in the hands.

Another name for Ankylosing Spondylitis. Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a type of arthritis of the spine. It causes inflammation (swelling) between your vertebrae (the bones that make up your spine) and the joints between your spine and pelvis.
A doctor who treats arthritis and autoimmune diseases.

Another name for Poison Ivy, Oak, and Sumac. If you spend time outdoors, chances are you have been bothered by poison ivy, poison oak or poison sumac at some point. Most people are sensitive to the plants' oily sap.

Another name for Progressive Supranuclear Palsy. Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is a rare brain disease. It happens because of damage to nerve cells in the brain. PSP affects your movement, including control of your walking and balance.
Rickets causes soft, weak bones in children. It usually occurs when they do not get enough vitamin D, which helps growing bones absorb the minerals calcium and phosphorous.

Another name for Heart Failure. Heart failure means that your heart can't pump enough oxygen-rich blood to meet your body's needs. Heart failure doesn't mean that your heart has stopped or is about to stop beating.

Another name for Tinea Infections. Tinea is the name of a group of diseases caused by a fungus. Types of tinea include ringworm, athlete's foot and jock itch. These infections are usually not serious, but they can be uncomfortable.
Something that raises your chance of getting a disease, such as smoking, high blood pressure or family history.

Another name for Restless Legs. Restless legs syndrome (RLS) causes a powerful urge to move your legs. Your legs become uncomfortable when you are lying down or sitting. Some people describe it as a creeping, crawling, tingling, or burning sensation.
Another name for Pesticides. Pests live where they are not wanted or cause harm to crops, people, or animals. Pesticides can help get rid of them. Pesticides are not just insect killers.
Rosacea is a long-term disease that affects your skin and sometimes your eyes. It causes redness and pimples. Rosacea is most common in women and people with fair skin.
A group of muscles and tendons that hold the shoulder joint in place and let you lift and turn your arm.
Your rotator cuff is part of your shoulder joint. It's a group of muscles and tendons that holds the top part of your upper arm bone firmly in your shoulder socket.

Rotavirus is a virus that causes gastroenteritis. Symptoms include severe diarrhea, vomiting, fever, and dehydration. Almost all children in the U.S. are likely to be infected with rotavirus before their 5th birthday.

Another name for Dietary Fiber. Fiber is a substance in plants. Dietary fiber is the kind you eat. It's a type of carbohydrate. You may also see it listed on a food label as soluble fiber or insoluble fiber.
Another name for Health Checkup. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
Respiratory syncytial virus: a common virus that causes cold-like symptoms but can be serious for babies and older adults. Vaccines and preventive shots are available.
Rubella is most dangerous for a pregnant woman's baby. It can cause miscarriage or birth defects.
Another name for Measles. Sometimes measles can lead to serious problems. There is no treatment for measles, but the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine can prevent it.

Another name for Herniated Disk. Your backbone, or spine, is made up of 26 bones called vertebrae. In between them are soft disks filled with a jelly-like substance. These disks cushion the vertebrae and keep them in place.
Around 15% of people in the United States live in rural areas. There are many different reasons why you might choose to live in a rural community.

Another name for Seasonal Affective Disorder. SAD is more common in women, young people, and those who live far from the equator. You are also more likely to have SAD if you or your family members have depression.
Opioids, sometimes called narcotics, are a type of drug. They include strong prescription pain relievers such as oxycodone, hydrocodone, fentanyl, and tramadol.
Young children are especially at risk. Supervision is the best way to keep them safe. Childproofing the house can also help.
Your salivary glands make saliva - sometimes called spit - and empty it into your mouth through openings called ducts. Saliva makes your food moist, which helps you chew and swallow.

Your salivary glands are in your mouth. You have three pairs of major salivary glands and hundreds of small (minor) glands. They make saliva (spit) and empty it into your mouth through openings called ducts.

Salmonella is the name of a group of bacteria. In the United States, it is a common cause of foodborne illness. Salmonella occurs in raw poultry, eggs, beef, and sometimes on unwashed fruit and vegetables.
Another name for Sodium. Table salt is a combination of two minerals - sodium and chloride Your body needs some sodium to work properly. It helps with the function of nerves and muscles.
Sarcoidosis is a condition in which groups of cells in your immune system form small, red, and swollen (inflamed) lumps. These lumps are called granulomas.
Another name for COVID-19 Testing. Even if your COVID-19 viral test is negative (the test did not detect the virus), you should still take steps to protect yourself and others.
A type of fat found mainly in meat, butter and cheese. Too much can raise LDL ('bad') cholesterol.

Another name for Sudden Cardiac Arrest. Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) is a condition in which the heart suddenly stops beating. When that happens, blood stops flowing to the brain and other vital organs.

Scabies is an itchy skin condition caused by the microscopic mite Sarcoptes scabei. It is common all over the world, and can affect anyone. Scabies spreads quickly in crowded conditions where there is frequent skin-to-skin contact between people.

A scar is a permanent patch of skin that grows over a wound. It forms when your body heals itself after a cut, scrape, burn, or sore. You can also get scars from surgery that cuts through the skin, infections like chickenpox, or skin conditions like acne.
A serious mental illness that affects how a person thinks, feels and acts, and may include hallucinations or false beliefs.
Your child spends more time at school than anywhere else except home. Schools can have a major effect on children's health. Schools can teach children about health, and promote healthy behaviors.
Pain that runs from the lower back down the back of one leg, caused by a pinched nerve.
Scleroderma means "hard skin." It's the name of an autoimmune disease that causes inflammation and thickening in the skin and other areas of the body.
A sideways curve of the spine.
A test to look for a disease before you have symptoms, so it can be treated early.
Another name for Health Screening. Screenings are tests that look for diseases before you have symptoms. Screening tests can find diseases early, when they're easier to treat.

Another name for Motion Sickness. Motion sickness is a common problem in people traveling by car, train, airplanes, and especially boats. Anyone can get it, but it is more common in children, pregnant women, and people taking certain medicines.
SAD is more common in women, young people, and those who live far from the equator. You are also more likely to have SAD if you or your family members have depression.

Another name for Seasonal Affective Disorder. SAD is more common in women, young people, and those who live far from the equator. You are also more likely to have SAD if you or your family members have depression.
Another name for Flu. The flu, also called influenza, is a respiratory infection caused by viruses. Each year, millions of Americans get sick with the flu. Sometimes it causes mild illness.

Another name for Seasonal Affective Disorder. SAD is more common in women, young people, and those who live far from the equator. You are also more likely to have SAD if you or your family members have depression.
Another name for Pinworms. Pinworms are small parasites that can live in the colon and rectum. You get them when you swallow their eggs. The eggs hatch inside your intestines.

Another name for Dandruff, Cradle Cap, and Other Scalp Conditions. Your scalp is the skin on the top of your head. Unless you have hair loss, hair grows on your scalp. Different skin problems can affect your scalp.

Another name for Dandruff, Cradle Cap, and Other Scalp Conditions. Your scalp is the skin on the top of your head. Unless you have hair loss, hair grows on your scalp. Different skin problems can affect your scalp.
Asking another doctor to review your diagnosis or treatment plan. It is your right and is common before big decisions.
Secondhand smoke is a mixture of the smoke that comes from the burning end of a cigarette, cigar, or pipe, and the smoke breathed out by the smoker.
Medicine that makes you calm, relaxed or sleepy during a procedure.
Sitting a lot and getting little physical activity. A sedentary lifestyle raises the risk of heart disease.

Another name for Health Risks of an Inactive Lifestyle. Being a couch potato. Not exercising. A sedentary or inactive lifestyle. These all mean the same thing: a lifestyle with a lot of sitting and lying down, with very little or no exercise.

Another name for Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome. Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a serious, long-term illness that affects many body systems. Another name for it is chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS).
A sudden burst of electrical activity in the brain that can cause shaking, staring or loss of awareness.

Seizures are symptoms of a brain problem. They happen because of sudden, abnormal electrical activity in the brain. When people think of seizures, they often think of convulsions in which a person's body shakes rapidly and uncontrollably.
Self-harm is not a mental disorder. It is a behavior - an unhealthy way to cope with strong feelings. However, some of the people who harm themselves do have a mental disorder.

Another name for Self-Harm. Self-harm is not a mental disorder. It is a behavior - an unhealthy way to cope with strong feelings. However, some of the people who harm themselves do have a mental disorder.
Another name for Dementia. It is normal to become a bit more forgetful as you age. But dementia is not a normal part of aging. It is a serious disorder that interferes with your daily life.

Another name for Older Adult Mental Health. Mental health includes our emotional, psychological, and social well-being. It affects how we think, feel, and act as we cope with life. It also helps determine how we handle stress, relate to others, and make choices.

Another name for Exercise for Older Adults. If you have not been active, you can start slowly and work up to your goal. How much exercise you need depends on your age and health. Check with your health care provider on what is right for you.
The body's extreme, life-threatening reaction to an infection. Signs include fever or low temperature, fast heartbeat, confusion and very fast breathing. Call 911.

Another name for Infectious Arthritis. One type of infectious arthritis is reactive arthritis. The reaction is to an infection somewhere else in your body. The joint is usually the knee, ankle, or toe.
The amount of food that the nutrition label numbers are based on.
Sexual assault is any kind of sexual activity, contact, or experience that happens without your consent. That means the sexual activity happens even though you don't agree to it.
Sexuality is a big part of being human. Love, affection and sexual intimacy all play a role in healthy relationships. They also contribute to your sense of well-being.

Stress, illness, medicines, or emotional problems may also be factors. Occasional problems with sexual function are common. If problems last more than a few months or cause distress for you or your partner, you should see your health care provider.
These problems may have physical or psychological causes. Physical causes may include conditions like diabetes, heart disease, nerve disorders, or hormone problems.

Another name for Sexually Transmitted Infections. Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are infections that are passed from one person to another through sexual contact. If not treated, an STI can develop into a sexually transmitted disease (STD).
Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are infections that are passed from one person to another through sexual contact. If not treated, an STI can develop into a sexually transmitted disease (STD).
Another name for Parkinson's Disease. Parkinson's disease (PD) is a type of movement disorder. It happens when nerve cells in the brain don't produce enough of a brain chemical called dopamine.
A painful rash with blisters, usually on one side of the body, caused by the chickenpox virus waking up again. A vaccine is recommended for adults 50 and older.
A dangerous condition where not enough blood reaches the organs. Signs include pale, cold, clammy skin, a fast pulse and confusion. Call 911.
Feeling that you cannot get enough air. Sudden or severe shortness of breath is an emergency.
Another name for Childhood Vaccines. Vaccines are injections (shots), liquids, pills, or nasal sprays that you take to teach the immune system to recognize and defend against harmful germs.
Your shoulder joint is composed of three bones: the clavicle (collarbone), the scapula (shoulder blade), and the humerus (upper arm bone). Your shoulders are the most movable joints in your body.

Another name for Sickle Cell Disease. Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a group of inherited red blood cell disorders. If you have SCD, there is a problem with your hemoglobin. Hemoglobin is a protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen throughout the body.
An inherited blood disease where red blood cells are shaped like a sickle (C shape), causing pain, anemia and infections.
An unwanted effect of a medicine or treatment, such as nausea or drowsiness.
Another name for Drug Reactions. Most of the time, medicines make our lives better. They reduce aches and pains, fight infections, and control problems such as high blood pressure or diabetes.
Sudden infant death syndrome: the unexplained death of a healthy baby during sleep. Putting babies to sleep on their backs, alone, in an empty crib lowers the risk.
Air-filled spaces in the bones of the face around the nose. Sinus infections cause stuffiness and face pain.
A sinus infection: swelling of the spaces around the nose, causing a stuffy nose, face pain and thick mucus.

Another name for Health Risks of an Inactive Lifestyle. Being a couch potato. Not exercising. A sedentary or inactive lifestyle. These all mean the same thing: a lifestyle with a lot of sitting and lying down, with very little or no exercise.

Sjögren's disease, previously called Sjögren's syndrome, is a chronic (long-lasting) autoimmune disease. When you have an autoimmune disease, your immune system attacks healthy tissues and organs by mistake.

Another name for Sjögren's Disease. Sjögren's disease, previously called Sjögren's syndrome, is a chronic (long-lasting) autoimmune disease. When you have an autoimmune disease, your immune system attacks healthy tissues and organs by mistake.
Your skin changes as you age. You might notice wrinkles, age spots and dryness. Your skin also becomes thinner and loses fat, making it less plump and smooth.
Cancer of the skin, usually from sun damage. Melanoma is the most serious kind.
NIH: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases
Your skin is your body's largest organ. It has many different functions, including covering and protecting your body. It helps keep germs out.
Pigmentation means coloring. Skin pigmentation disorders affect the color of your skin. Your skin gets its color from a pigment called melanin.
Another name for Rashes. A rash is an area of irritated or swollen skin. Many rashes are itchy, red, painful, and irritated. Some rashes can also lead to blisters or patches of raw skin.

Another name for Head Injuries. Chances are you've bumped your head before. Often, the injury is minor because your skull is hard and it protects your brain. But other head injuries can be more severe, such as a skull fracture, concussion, or traumatic brain injury.

Another name for Head Injuries. Chances are you've bumped your head before. Often, the injury is minor because your skull is hard and it protects your brain. But other head injuries can be more severe, such as a skull fracture, concussion, or traumatic brain injury.

Another name for Steatotic Liver Disease. Your liver is the largest organ inside your body. It helps you digest food, store energy, and remove harmful substances (toxins). Steatotic liver disease, formerly called fatty liver disease, happens when too much fat builds up in your liver.
Another name for Lupus. Lupus is a chronic (long-lasting) type of autoimmune disease. Autoimmune diseases happen when your immune system attacks healthy cells and tissues by mistake.
A condition where breathing stops and starts many times during sleep, often with loud snoring. It raises the risk of high blood pressure and heart problems.
While you are sleeping your brain and body functions are still active. Sleep is a natural process that helps your body restore energy, supports learning and memory, and keeps you healthy.
Habits that help you sleep well, such as a regular bedtime, a dark quiet room and no screens before bed.
A test, often overnight, that records your breathing, heart rate and brain waves while you sleep. It is used to find sleep apnea.
Another name for Sleep Apnea. Sleep apnea is a common disorder that causes your breathing to stop or get very shallow. Breathing pauses can last from a few seconds to minutes.
Prices that go up or down based on your income, used by many community clinics.

Another name for Herniated Disk. Your backbone, or spine, is made up of 26 bones called vertebrae. In between them are soft disks filled with a jelly-like substance. These disks cushion the vertebrae and keep them in place.

Another name for Spinal Muscular Atrophy. Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a group of genetic diseases that damages and kills motor neurons. Motor neurons are a type of nerve cell in the spinal cord and lower part of the brain.

Another name for Heroin. Heroin is an illegal, very addictive opioid drug. It's made from morphine, which comes from the seedpod of opium poppy plants. These plants grow in Southeast and Southwest Asia, Mexico, and Colombia.

Another name for Intestinal Cancer. Your small intestine is part of your digestive system. It is a long tube that connects your stomach to your large intestine. Intestinal cancer is rare, but eating a high-fat diet or having Crohn's disease, celiac disease, or a history of colonic polyps can increase your risk.

Your small intestine is the longest part of your digestive system - about twenty feet long! It connects your stomach to your large intestine (or colon) and folds many times to fit inside your abdomen.
Smallpox is a disease caused by the Variola major virus. Some experts say that over the centuries it has killed more people than all other infectious diseases combined.
Recent research shows the dangers of smokeless tobacco may go beyond the mouth. It might also play a role in other cancers, heart disease and stroke.

There's no way around it; smoking is bad for your health. It harms nearly every organ of the body, even some that you would not expect. Cigarette smoking causes many cancers and other health problems.

Smoking cigarettes has many health risks for everyone. However, the younger you are when you start smoking, the more problems it can cause. People who start smoking before the age of 21 have the hardest time quitting.
Quitting smoking. It lowers the risk of heart attack and stroke within a few years. Free help is available at 1-800-QUIT-NOW.
Snoring is the sound you make when your breathing is blocked while you are asleep. The sound is caused by tissues at the top of your airway that strike each other and vibrate.

Another name for Cocaine. Cocaine is a very addictive drug that is made from leaves of the coca plant found in South America. It is mostly available as an illegal drug that some people use to get high.
Another name for Smokeless Tobacco. Recent research shows the dangers of smokeless tobacco may go beyond the mouth. It might also play a role in other cancers, heart disease and stroke.
Having little contact with other people. It is common in older adults and is linked to poorer health.
A professional who helps patients and families with things like insurance, housing, home care and emotional support.

Another name for Cocaine. Cocaine is a very addictive drug that is made from leaves of the coca plant found in South America. It is mostly available as an illegal drug that some people use to get high.
Salt is the main source of sodium in food. Too much sodium raises blood pressure, so people with heart problems are often told to eat less of it.
Your soft tissues connect, support, or surround other tissues. Examples include your muscles, tendons, fat, and blood vessels. Soft tissue sarcoma is a cancer of these soft tissues.
Pain or scratchiness in the throat, often from a cold or other infection.

Another name for Chagas Disease. Chagas disease, or American trypanosomiasis, is an illness that can cause serious heart and stomach problems. It is caused by a parasite. Chagas disease is common in Latin America, especially in poor, rural areas.
Another name for Croup. Croup is an inflammation of the vocal cords (larynx) and windpipe (trachea). It causes difficulty breathing, a barking cough, and a hoarse voice.
A doctor trained in one area of medicine, such as the heart or skin.
Some speech and communication problems may be genetic. Often, no one knows the causes. By first grade, about 5% of children have noticeable speech disorders.

term: Speech and Language Problems in Children
meaning: Children vary in their development of speech and language skills. Health care professionals have lists of milestones for what's normal. These milestones help figure out whether a child is on track or if he or she may need extra help.
Therapy that helps with speaking, understanding language or swallowing, for example after a stroke.
Another name for Methamphetamine. Methamphetamine - meth for short - is a very addictive stimulant drug. It is a powder that can be made into a pill or a shiny rock (called a crystal).
Though many people are afraid of spiders, they rarely bite people unless threatened. Most spider bites are harmless. Occasionally, spider bites can cause allergic reactions.

Spina bifida is a neural tube defect - a type of birth defect of the brain, spine, or spinal cord. It happens if the spinal column of the fetus doesn't close completely during the first month of pregnancy.
The bundle of nerves that runs down the inside of the backbone, carrying messages between the brain and body.
Symptoms vary but might include pain, numbness, loss of sensation and muscle weakness. These symptoms can occur around the spinal cord, and also in other areas such as your arms and legs.
Your spinal cord is a bundle of nerves that runs down the middle of your back. It carries signals back and forth between your body and your brain.
Another name for Meningitis. Meningitis is inflammation of the thin tissue that surrounds the brain and spinal cord, called the meninges. There are several types of meningitis.
Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a group of genetic diseases that damages and kills motor neurons. Motor neurons are a type of nerve cell in the spinal cord and lower part of the brain.

Your spine, or backbone, protects your spinal cord and allows you to stand and bend. Spinal stenosis causes narrowing in your spine. The narrowing puts pressure on your nerves and spinal cord and can cause pain.
The backbone: a column of small bones (vertebrae) that supports the body and protects the spinal cord.

Spinal diseases often cause pain when bone changes put pressure on the spinal cord or nerves. They can also limit movement. Treatments differ by disease, but sometimes they include back braces and surgery.
A breathing test where you blow hard into a tube to measure how well your lungs work.
Another name for Smokeless Tobacco. Recent research shows the dangers of smokeless tobacco may go beyond the mouth. It might also play a role in other cancers, heart disease and stroke.
An organ on the upper left side of the belly that filters blood and helps fight infection.

Your spleen is an organ above your stomach and under your ribs on your left side. It is about as big as your fist. The spleen is part of your lymphatic system, which fights infection and keeps your body fluids in balance.

Another name for Spleen Diseases. Your spleen is an organ above your stomach and under your ribs on your left side. It is about as big as your fist. The spleen is part of your lymphatic system, which fights infection and keeps your body fluids in balance.
A support that holds an injured body part still, often used before a cast or for a sprain.

Another name for Miscarriage. A miscarriage is an unexpected loss of pregnancy before the 20th week. Most miscarriages happen very early in the pregnancy, often before a woman even knows she is pregnant.
Sports can be a great way to get in shape or stay that way. Having a specific goal can be a great motivator. Physically, you need strength and endurance.
Exercising is good for you, but sometimes you can injure yourself when you play sports or exercise. Accidents, poor training practices, or improper gear can cause them.

If you have already hurt yourself playing a sport, make sure you recover completely before you start up again. If possible, protect the injured part of your body with padding, a brace, or special equipment.

Another name for Intimate Partner Violence. Intimate partner violence (IPV) is abuse that happens in a romantic relationship. The intimate partner could be a current or former spouse or dating partner.
A stretched or torn ligament (the tissue that holds bones together at a joint), often in the ankle or wrist.
A sprain is a stretched or torn ligament. Ligaments are tissues that connect bones at a joint. Falling, twisting, or getting hit can all cause a sprain.
Finding out how big a cancer is and how far it has spread. Stages usually go from 1 (early) to 4 (spread).
Another name for Stuttering. Sometimes, along with the stuttering, there may be nodding, rapid blinking, or trembling lips. The stuttering may be worse when you are stressed, excited, or tired.
Another name for Staphylococcal Infections. Staphylococcus (staph) is a group of bacteria. There are more than 30 types. A type called Staphylococcus aureus causes most infections.
Staphylococcus (staph) is a group of bacteria. There are more than 30 types. A type called Staphylococcus aureus causes most infections.
A type of medicine (such as atorvastatin) that lowers 'bad' LDL cholesterol and lowers the risk of heart attack and stroke.

Cholesterol is a waxy, fat-like substance that's found in all the cells in your body. Your body needs some cholesterol to work properly. But if you have too much of it in your blood, it can stick to the walls of your arteries and narrow or even block them.

Another name for How to Improve Mental Health. Mental health includes our emotional, psychological, and social well-being. It affects how we think, feel, and act as we cope with life. It also helps determine how we handle stress, relate to others, and make choices.
Sexually transmitted disease (also called STI): an infection passed through sexual contact, such as chlamydia, gonorrhea or HIV.

Another name for Sexually Transmitted Infections. Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are infections that are passed from one person to another through sexual contact. If not treated, an STI can develop into a sexually transmitted disease (STD).

Your liver is the largest organ inside your body. It helps you digest food, store energy, and remove harmful substances (toxins). Steatotic liver disease, formerly called fatty liver disease, happens when too much fat builds up in your liver.

Another name for Progressive Supranuclear Palsy. Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is a rare brain disease. It happens because of damage to nerve cells in the brain. PSP affects your movement, including control of your walking and balance.

Another name for Polycystic Ovary Syndrome. Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), also known as polyendocrine metabolic ovary syndrome (PMOS), is the name of a hormonal disorder. PCOS affects the ovaries, as well as many other parts of the body.
Stem cells are cells with the potential to develop into many different types of cells in the body. They serve as a repair system for the body.
A tiny mesh tube placed in a blood vessel to keep it open.
Free of germs. Also means unable to have children.

Another name for Infertility. Infertility means not becoming pregnant after having frequent, unprotected sex for one year or longer. If you are age 35 or older, infertility can be diagnosed after six months.
You may have heard of anabolic steroids, which can have harmful effects. But there's another type of steroid - sometimes called a corticosteroid - that treats a variety of problems.
The tool a doctor uses to listen to your heart and lungs.
Another name for Juvenile Arthritis. Juvenile arthritis (JA) is arthritis that happens in children. It causes joint inflammation (swelling), pain, stiffness, and loss of motion.
In many cases, the cause remains unknown. Some causes may be preventable, but most are not.

Another name for Sexually Transmitted Infections. Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are infections that are passed from one person to another through sexual contact. If not treated, an STI can develop into a sexually transmitted disease (STD).
Threads used to close a cut or surgical wound. Also called sutures.
It is hard to diagnose stomach cancer in its early stages. Indigestion and stomach discomfort can be symptoms of early cancer, but other problems can cause the same symptoms.
Your stomach is an organ between your esophagus and small intestine. It is where digestion of protein begins. The stomach has three tasks. It stores swallowed food.

Another name for Gastroenteritis. Gastroenteritis is an inflammation of the lining of the stomach and intestines. The main symptoms include vomiting and diarrhea. It is usually not serious in healthy people, but it can sometimes lead to dehydration or cause severe symptoms.

Another name for Peptic Ulcer. Peptic ulcers happen when the acids that help you digest food damage the walls of the stomach or duodenum. The most common cause is infection with a bacterium called Helicobacter pylori.
Another name for Bowel Movement. A bowel movement is the last stop in the movement of food through your digestive tract. Your stool passes out of your body through the rectum and anus.

Another name for Bowel Incontinence. Bowel incontinence is the inability to control your bowels. When you feel the urge to have a bowel movement, you may not be able to hold it until you get to a toilet.
A test of a small sample of poop, used to look for blood, infection or signs of colon cancer.

Another name for Streptococcal Infections. Strep is short for Streptococcus, a type of bacteria that often lives in your nose and throat. Most strep infections are mild, but some may become serious depending on your overall health.
A throat infection caused by strep bacteria, with a very sore throat and fever. It needs antibiotics.
Strep is short for Streptococcus, a type of bacteria that often lives in your nose and throat. Most strep infections are mild, but some may become serious depending on your overall health.

Another name for Pneumococcal Infections. How the diagnosis is made depends upon where the infection is. Your doctor will do a physical exam and ask about your medical history. Possible tests may include blood, imaging, or lab tests.
The body's and mind's reaction to pressure or challenges. Long-term stress can harm your health.
A test that checks how the heart works during exercise, usually walking on a treadmill while connected to an EKG. Medicine can be used instead of exercise.
When blood flow to part of the brain is blocked or a blood vessel bursts. Signs (BE FAST): face drooping, arm weakness, speech trouble. Call 911 right away.
Stroke rehabilitation is a program for people who have had a stroke. A stroke happens when there is a loss of blood flow to part of the brain.
Sometimes, along with the stuttering, there may be nodding, rapid blinking, or trembling lips. The stuttering may be worse when you are stressed, excited, or tired.
Another name for Lupus. Lupus is a chronic (long-lasting) type of autoimmune disease. Autoimmune diseases happen when your immune system attacks healthy cells and tissues by mistake.

Another name for Hemorrhagic Stroke. A stroke happens when there is a loss of blood flow to part of the brain. Your brain cells cannot get the oxygen and nutrients they need from blood, and they start to die within a few minutes.
Help from the government to lower the cost of health insurance, for example through the Health Insurance Marketplace.

Another name for Drug Use and Addiction. Drugs are chemical substances that can change how your body and mind work. They include prescription medicines, over-the-counter medicines, alcohol, tobacco, and illegal drugs.
When using alcohol or drugs causes problems in a person's life but they cannot stop. It is a treatable medical condition.
Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) is a condition in which the heart suddenly stops beating. When that happens, blood stops flowing to the brain and other vital organs.

Sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS) is the sudden, unexplained death of an infant younger than one year old. Some people call SIDS "crib death" because many babies who die of SIDS are found in their cribs.
Thinking about ending your life. If you or someone you know has these thoughts, call or text 988 or call 911 right away.

Suicide is the taking of one's own life. It is a death that happens when someone harms themselves because they want to end their life. A suicide attempt is when someone harms themselves to try to end their life, but they do not die.
Ultraviolet (UV) rays are an invisible form of radiation. They can pass through your skin and damage your skin cells. Sunburns are a sign of skin damage.
Red, painful skin from too much sun. Sunburns raise the risk of skin cancer.
Another name for Heat Illness. Your body normally cools itself by sweating. During hot weather, especially when it is very humid, sweating just isn't enough to cool you off.
A vitamin, mineral, herb or other product taken to add to your diet. Tell your doctor about supplements because some interact with medicines.
Another name for Hidradenitis Suppurativa. Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) is a chronic skin disease. Another name for it is acne inversa. It causes painful, boil-like lumps that form under the skin.
A doctor who does operations.
There are many reasons to have surgery. Some operations can relieve or prevent pain. Others can reduce a symptom of a problem or improve some body function.
An unexpected bill, often from an out-of-network doctor at an in-network hospital. U.S. law (the No Surprises Act) protects you from many of these.
If you have a swallowing disorder, you may have difficulty or pain when swallowing. Some people cannot swallow at all. Others may have trouble swallowing liquids, foods, or saliva.
Sweat is a clear, salty liquid produced by glands in your skin. Sweating is how your body cools itself. You sweat mainly under your arms and on your feet and palms.
When part of the body gets bigger than normal, often from fluid or inflammation.

Another name for H1N1 Flu (Swine Flu). Swine flu is an infection caused by a virus. It's named for a virus that pigs can get. People do not normally get swine flu, but human infections can and do happen.
A change in your body or how you feel that may be a sign of illness, such as pain or fever.
The medical word for fainting: a short loss of consciousness, usually from a drop in blood flow to the brain.
A group of symptoms that happen together and point to a particular condition.
Syphilis is a sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by bacteria. It infects the genital area, lips, mouth, or anus of both men and women.
Symptoms vary according to the size and location of the syrinx. They often begin in early adulthood.

Another name for Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome. Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a serious, long-term illness that affects many body systems. Another name for it is chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS).
Another name for Lupus. Lupus is a chronic (long-lasting) type of autoimmune disease. Autoimmune diseases happen when your immune system attacks healthy cells and tissues by mistake.
Another name for Scleroderma. Scleroderma means "hard skin." It's the name of an autoimmune disease that causes inflammation and thickening in the skin and other areas of the body.
The top number in a blood pressure reading. It measures the pressure in the arteries when the heart beats.
A pill: medicine pressed into a small solid shape.
A heart rate that is faster than normal, usually over 100 beats a minute while resting.
The tailbone is the small bone at the bottom of your backbone, or spine. Tailbone disorders include tailbone injuries, pain, infections, cysts and tumors.
Some people think that tanning gives them a healthy glow. But tanning, either outdoors or indoors with a tanning bed, is not healthy at all.
Our senses of taste and smell give us great pleasure. Taste helps us enjoy food and beverages. Smell lets us enjoy the scents and fragrances like roses or coffee.
Transcatheter aortic valve replacement: putting in a new aortic valve through a tube in a blood vessel, without opening the chest.
Tay-Sachs disease is a rare, inherited disease. It is a type of lipid metabolism disorder. It causes too much of a fatty substance to build up in the brain.
Another name for Tuberculosis. Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial disease that usually attacks the lungs. But it can also attack other parts of the body, including the kidneys, spine, and brain.
Another name for Traumatic Brain Injury. Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a sudden injury that causes damage to the brain. It may happen when there is a blow, bump, or jolt to the head.

Another name for Tetanus, Diphtheria, and Pertussis Vaccines. Some people should not get these vaccines, including those who have had severe reactions to the shots before. Check with your health care provider first if you have seizures, a neurologic problem, or Guillain-Barre syndrome.

Another name for Tetanus, Diphtheria, and Pertussis Vaccines. Some people should not get these vaccines, including those who have had severe reactions to the shots before. Check with your health care provider first if you have seizures, a neurologic problem, or Guillain-Barre syndrome.
A vaccine that protects against tetanus, diphtheria and whooping cough (pertussis). Adults get a booster every 10 years, and during each pregnancy.
You may only think of tears as those salty drops that fall from your eyes when you cry. Actually, your tears clean your eyes every time you blink.

Depression in teens (ages 13-17) is a serious medical illness. It's more than just a feeling of being sad or "blue" for a few days. It is an intense feeling of sadness, hopelessness, and anger or frustration that lasts much longer.
As a teenager, you go through many physical, mental, emotional, and social changes. The biggest change is puberty, the process of becoming sexually mature.

Another name for Drugs and Young People. Young people's brains are growing and developing until they are their mid-20's. This is especially true of the prefrontal cortex, which is used to make decisions.
As a teenager, you go through many changes. Your body is on its way to becoming its adult size. You may notice that you can't fit into your old shoes or that your jeans are now 3 inches too short.

Being a teenager is hard. You're under stress to be liked, do well in school, get along with your family, and make big decisions. You can't avoid most of these pressures, and worrying about them is normal.
Teen sexual health is about how sex affects your physical and emotional health. It means knowing how to form healthy relationships and making decisions about sex that are right for you.

Another name for Smoking and Youth. Smoking cigarettes has many health risks for everyone. However, the younger you are when you start smoking, the more problems it can cause. People who start smoking before the age of 21 have the hardest time quitting.
Teen violence refers to harmful behaviors that can start early and continue into young adulthood. The young person can be a victim, an offender, or a witness to the violence.

Another name for Underage Drinking. Kids often begin drinking to look "cool" or fit in with their peers. Parents can help their kids avoid alcohol problems. Open communication and conversations about drinking are important.

Most teenage girls don't plan to get pregnant, but many do. Teen pregnancies carry extra health risks to both the mother and the baby. Often, teens don't get prenatal care soon enough, which can lead to problems later on.
When a baby's teeth start to come through the gums, causing drooling, fussiness and chewing.
Seeing a doctor or nurse by video or phone instead of in person.

Another name for Telehealth. Sometimes people use the term telemedicine to mean the same thing as telehealth. Telehealth is a broader term. It includes telemedicine. But it also includes things like training for health care providers, health care administrative meetings, and services provided by pharmacists and social workers.
How hot your body is. Normal body temperature is about 98.6°F (37°C); 100.4°F (38°C) or higher is a fever.
Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are a group of more than 30 conditions that affect your temporomandibular joints (TMJs). You have two TMJs; one on each side of your jaw.

Another name for Temporomandibular Disorders. Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are a group of more than 30 conditions that affect your temporomandibular joints (TMJs). You have two TMJs; one on each side of your jaw.
Painful swelling of a tendon, often from overuse.
A tough cord of tissue that attaches a muscle to a bone.
Another name for Tendinitis. Tendons are flexible bands of tissue that connect muscles to bones. They help your muscles move your bones. Tendinitis is the severe swelling of a tendon.
An illness that cannot be cured and is expected to lead to death.

Another name for End of Life Issues. Planning for the end of life can be difficult. But by deciding what end-of-life care best suits your needs when you are healthy, you can help those close to you make the right choices when the time comes.
Testicular cancer is a cancer that develops in the tissues of one or both testicles. The testicles, or testes, are part of the male reproductive system.
Testicles, or testes, make male hormones and sperm. They are two egg-shaped organs inside the scrotum, the loose sac of skin behind the penis.
A serious infection from bacteria entering a wound, causing stiff, painful muscles. Prevented by a vaccine every 10 years.

Another name for Tetanus, Diphtheria, and Pertussis Vaccines. Some people should not get these vaccines, including those who have had severe reactions to the shots before. Check with your health care provider first if you have seizures, a neurologic problem, or Guillain-Barre syndrome.

Thalassemias are inherited blood disorders. If you have one, your body makes fewer healthy red blood cells and less hemoglobin. Hemoglobin is a protein that carries oxygen to the body.
Another name for Gonorrhea. Gonorrhea is a sexually transmitted infection (STI). It is most common in young adults. The bacteria that cause gonorrhea can infect the genital tract, mouth, or anus.

Another name for Diarrhea. Diarrhea is loose, watery stools (bowel movements). You have diarrhea if you have loose stools three or more times in one day. Acute diarrhea is diarrhea that lasts a short time.

Another name for Diarrhea. Diarrhea is loose, watery stools (bowel movements). You have diarrhea if you have loose stools three or more times in one day. Acute diarrhea is diarrhea that lasts a short time.

Another name for How to Lower Cholesterol with Diet. Cholesterol is a waxy, fat-like substance that's found in all the cells in your body. Your body needs some cholesterol to work properly. But if you have too much of it in your blood, it can stick to the walls of your arteries and narrow or even block them.
A trained professional who helps with mental health through talking, or with movement and daily tasks through physical or occupational therapy.
Thoracic outlet syndrome (TOS) causes pain in the shoulder, arm, and neck. It happens when the nerves or blood vessels just below your neck are compressed, or squeezed.
Another name for Pinworms. Pinworms are small parasites that can live in the colon and rectum. You get them when you swallow their eggs. The eggs hatch inside your intestines.
Another name for Rubella. Rubella is most dangerous for a pregnant woman's baby. It can cause miscarriage or birth defects.

Throat cancer is a type of head and neck cancer. Throat cancer has different names, depending on which part of the throat is affected. The different parts of your throat are called the oropharynx, the hypopharynx, the nasopharynx, and the larynx, or voice box.
Your throat is a tube that carries food to your esophagus and air to your windpipe and larynx. The technical name for your throat is the pharynx.
Another name for Platelet Disorders. NIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
When a blood clot forms inside a blood vessel and blocks it.

Another name for Ischemic Stroke. A stroke happens when there is a loss of blood flow to part of the brain. Your brain cells cannot get the oxygen and nutrients they need from blood, and they start to die within a few minutes.

Another name for Heroin. Heroin is an illegal, very addictive opioid drug. It's made from morphine, which comes from the seedpod of opium poppy plants. These plants grow in Southeast and Southwest Asia, Mexico, and Colombia.
Another name for Thymus Cancer. The thymus is a small organ in your upper chest, under your breastbone. Before birth and during childhood, the thymus helps the body make a type of white blood cell.
The thymus is a small organ in your upper chest, under your breastbone. Before birth and during childhood, the thymus helps the body make a type of white blood cell.
A gland in the neck that makes hormones controlling energy and metabolism.
Thyroid cancer is a cancer that starts in the tissues of the thyroid. Your thyroid is a small, butterfly-shaped gland in the front of your neck.

Your thyroid is a small, butterfly-shaped gland in the front of your neck. It makes hormones that control the way the body uses energy. These hormones affect nearly every organ in your body and control many of your body's most important functions.

Your thyroid is a small, butterfly-shaped gland in the front of your neck. It makes hormones that control the way the body uses energy. These hormones affect nearly every organ in your body and control many of your body's most important functions.

Another name for Transient Ischemic Attack. Most symptoms of a TIA disappear within an hour, although they may last for up to 24 hours. Because you cannot tell if these symptoms are from a TIA or a stroke, you should go to the hospital right away.

Another name for Trigeminal Neuralgia. Trigeminal neuralgia (TN) is a type of chronic pain that affects your face. It causes extreme, sudden burning or shock-like pain. It usually affects one side of the face.
Ticks are small parasites. They may look like insects, but they have eight legs and are related to spiders. Ticks feed on the blood of people and warm-blooded animals.
On a prescription, means three times a day, often with meals.
Another name for Methamphetamine. Methamphetamine - meth for short - is a very addictive stimulant drug. It is a powder that can be made into a pill or a shiny rock (called a crystal).
Tinea is the name of a group of diseases caused by a fungus. Types of tinea include ringworm, athlete's foot and jock itch. These infections are usually not serious, but they can be uncomfortable.

Another name for Athlete's Foot. Athlete's foot is a common infection caused by a fungus. It most often affects the space between the toes. Symptoms include itching, burning, and cracked, scaly skin between your toes.
A pins-and-needles feeling, often in the hands or feet.
Ringing, buzzing or hissing in the ears when there is no outside sound.

Another name for Fatigue. Fatigue is a feeling of weariness, tiredness, or lack of energy. It can interfere with your usual daily activities. Fatigue can be a normal response to physical activity, emotional stress, boredom, or lack of sleep.
A group of similar cells that work together, such as muscle tissue or skin.

Another name for How to Lower Cholesterol with Diet. Cholesterol is a waxy, fat-like substance that's found in all the cells in your body. Your body needs some cholesterol to work properly. But if you have too much of it in your blood, it can stick to the walls of your arteries and narrow or even block them.

Another name for Temporomandibular Disorders. Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are a group of more than 30 conditions that affect your temporomandibular joints (TMJs). You have two TMJs; one on each side of your jaw.

Another name for Temporomandibular Disorders. Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are a group of more than 30 conditions that affect your temporomandibular joints (TMJs). You have two TMJs; one on each side of your jaw.

Another name for Trigeminal Neuralgia. Trigeminal neuralgia (TN) is a type of chronic pain that affects your face. It causes extreme, sudden burning or shock-like pain. It usually affects one side of the face.
Another name for Secondhand Smoke. Secondhand smoke is a mixture of the smoke that comes from the burning end of a cigarette, cigar, or pipe, and the smoke breathed out by the smoker.

Another name for Smoking. There's no way around it; smoking is bad for your health. It harms nearly every organ of the body, even some that you would not expect. Cigarette smoking causes many cancers and other health problems.
Toddlers do not develop at the same rate. There is a wide range of what is considered "normal." Your child may be ahead in some areas and slightly behind in others.
Most young children get sick. It is hard for parents to know what is serious. You can learn what the common warning signs are. In the end, trust your intuition.
Food provides the energy and nutrients that young children need to be healthy. Toddlers are learning to feed themselves and to eat new foods.

Fourteen of the 26 bones in your feet are in your toes. The toes, particularly your big toe, help you move and keep your balance. Playing sports, running, stubbing your toe, and dropping something on your foot can damage your toes.
Your tongue helps you taste, swallow, and chew. You also use it to speak. Your tongue is made up of many muscles. The upper surface contains your taste buds.
Another name for Tonsillitis. Tonsils are lumps of tissue at the back of the throat. There are two of them, one on each side. Along with the adenoids, tonsils are part of the lymphatic system.
Surgery to remove the tonsils.
Swollen, infected tonsils, causing a sore throat and trouble swallowing.
Two lumps of tissue at the back of the throat that help fight infection.

Tooth decay is damage to a tooth's surface, or enamel. It happens when bacteria in your mouth make acids that attack the enamel. Tooth decay can lead to cavities (dental caries), which are holes in your teeth.
You need your teeth for many activities that you may take for granted. These include eating, speaking and even smiling.
Put on the skin, such as a cream or ointment.
Tornadoes are nature's most violent storms. They are rotating, funnel-shaped clouds that extend from a thunderstorm to the ground. Their whirling winds can reach 300 miles per hour.

Another name for Thoracic Outlet Syndrome. Thoracic outlet syndrome (TOS) causes pain in the shoulder, arm, and neck. It happens when the nerves or blood vessels just below your neck are compressed, or squeezed.
If you have Tourette syndrome, you make unusual movements or sounds, called tics. You have little or no control over them. Common tics are throat-clearing and blinking.
A tight band wrapped around an arm or leg above a wound to stop severe bleeding.

Another name for Poison Ivy, Oak, and Sumac. If you spend time outdoors, chances are you have been bothered by poison ivy, poison oak or poison sumac at some point. Most people are sensitive to the plants' oily sap.
Toxoplasmosis is a disease caused by the parasite Toxoplasma gondii. More than 60 million people in the U.S. have the parasite. Most of them don't get sick.
Another name for Nutritional Support. You receive nutritional support through a needle or catheter placed in your vein or with a feeding tube, which goes into your stomach.
The windpipe: the tube that carries air from the throat to the lungs.
Your trachea, or windpipe, is one part of your airway system. Airways are pipes that carry oxygen-rich air to your lungs. They also carry carbon dioxide, a waste gas, out of your lungs.
A surgical opening in the front of the neck into the windpipe, with a tube to help a person breathe.
An unhealthy fat in some fried and packaged foods that raises 'bad' cholesterol and lowers 'good' cholesterol.
A 'mini-stroke' (TIA): stroke signs that go away within minutes or hours. It is a warning sign of a stroke and needs urgent care.
A physical injury, or deep emotional harm from a frightening or painful event.
Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a sudden injury that causes damage to the brain. It may happen when there is a blow, bump, or jolt to the head.

Another name for Wounds and Injuries. An injury is damage to your body. It is a general term that refers to harm caused by accidents, falls, hits, weapons, and more. In the U.S., millions of people injure themselves every year.

Traveling can increase your chances of getting sick. A long flight can increase your risk for deep vein thrombosis. Once you arrive, it takes time to adjust to the water, food, and air in another place.
A tremor is a neurological condition that includes shaking or trembling movements in one or more parts of your body. It most often affects the hands.
Sorting patients by how urgent their condition is, so the sickest are seen first.
Another name for Trichomoniasis. Trichomoniasis is a sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by a parasite. It spreads from person to person during sex. Many people do not have any symptoms.
Trichomoniasis is a sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by a parasite. It spreads from person to person during sex. Many people do not have any symptoms.
Trigeminal neuralgia (TN) is a type of chronic pain that affects your face. It causes extreme, sudden burning or shock-like pain. It usually affects one side of the face.
A type of fat in the blood. High levels raise the risk of heart disease and are measured in a lipid panel.
One of three periods of pregnancy, each about three months long.
Another name for Down Syndrome. Down syndrome is a condition in which a person has an extra chromosome or an extra piece of a chromosome. This extra copy changes how a baby's body and brain develop.
A protein released into the blood when the heart muscle is damaged. A blood test for troponin helps diagnose a heart attack.

Another name for Tuberous Sclerosis. Some people have signs of tuberous sclerosis at birth. In others it can take time for the symptoms to develop. The disease can be mild, or it can cause severe disabilities.
Thyroid-stimulating hormone. A blood test for TSH is the main check for thyroid problems.

A tsunami is a series of huge ocean waves created by an underwater disturbance. Causes include earthquakes, landslides, volcanic eruptions, or meteorites--chunks of rock from space that strike the surface of Earth.
Tubal ligation (getting your "tubes tied") is a type of surgery. It prevents a woman from getting pregnant. It is a permanent form of birth control, and is effective right away.
Another name for Ectopic Pregnancy. The uterus, or womb, is the place where a fetus grows during pregnancy. In an ectopic pregnancy, the fertilized egg grows in the wrong place outside the uterus.
Another name for Nutritional Support. You receive nutritional support through a needle or catheter placed in your vein or with a feeding tube, which goes into your stomach.
TB: a contagious bacterial infection that usually affects the lungs. Treatable with months of antibiotics.
Some people have signs of tuberous sclerosis at birth. In others it can take time for the symptoms to develop. The disease can be mild, or it can cause severe disabilities.

Another name for Tuberous Sclerosis. Some people have signs of tuberous sclerosis at birth. In others it can take time for the symptoms to develop. The disease can be mild, or it can cause severe disabilities.
An abnormal lump of tissue. It can be benign (not cancer) or malignant (cancer).

Tumors during pregnancy are rare, but they can happen. Tumors can be either benign (not cancer) or malignant (cancer). The most common cancers in pregnancy include breast cancer, thyroid cancer, cervical cancer, lymphoma, and melanoma.
Turner syndrome is a genetic disorder that affects a girl's development and appearance. It can also cause health problems such as infertility and heart problems.
If you are pregnant with more than one baby, you are far from alone. Multiple births are up in the United States. More women are having babies after age 30 and more are taking fertility drugs.
A type of diabetes where the body makes little or no insulin. People with it need insulin every day.
The most common type of diabetes, where the body does not use insulin well. It is treated with healthy eating, exercise and medicine.

Another name for Diabetes Type 1. Diabetes means your blood glucose, also called blood sugar, is too high. With type 1 diabetes, your body makes little or no insulin. Insulin is a hormone from your pancreas that helps glucose move from your body into your cells, where it is used for energy.
Another name for Hurricanes. A hurricane is a severe type of tropical storm. Hurricanes produce high winds, heavy rains and thunderstorms. Hurricanes can cause tremendous damage.

Another name for Urinalysis. A urinalysis is a test of your urine. It is often done to check for a urinary tract infection, kidney problems, or diabetes. You may also have one during a checkup, if you are admitted to the hospital, before you have surgery, or if you are pregnant.
An open sore on the skin or inside the body, such as in the stomach.
A long-term disease that causes inflammation and sores in the lining of the colon, with diarrhea, often bloody.

Another name for Ulcerative Colitis. Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a disease that causes inflammation and sores, called ulcers, in the lining of the rectum and colon. It is one of a group of diseases called inflammatory bowel disease.
A scan that uses sound waves to make pictures inside the body, often used during pregnancy.
It can be scary when your baby is sick, especially when it is not an everyday problem like a cold or a fever. You may not know whether the problem is serious or how to treat it.
Not awake and not able to respond. Call 911.
Another name for Hypothyroidism. Hypothyroidism, or underactive thyroid, happens when your thyroid gland doesn't make enough thyroid hormones to meet your body's needs.
Kids often begin drinking to look "cool" or fit in with their peers. Parents can help their kids avoid alcohol problems. Open communication and conversations about drinking are important.
It can be helpful to stay informed about new medical findings. But it's good to have some skepticism. Keep these questions in mind the next time you hear about a big new medical breakthrough.
Losing weight without trying. It should be checked by a doctor.
On one side of the body only.
Not having health insurance.

Another name for Depression. Depression is more than a feeling of being sad or irritable for a few days. It's a serious mood disorder. As one of the most common mental disorders in the United States, depression can affect how you think, feel, and your everyday life.
Chest pain that is new, getting worse or happens at rest. It can mean a heart attack is coming and needs emergency care.

Another name for Indigestion. Nearly everyone has had indigestion at one time. It's a feeling of discomfort or a burning feeling in your upper abdomen. You may have heartburn or belch and feel bloated.
One of two tubes that carry urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
Your kidneys make urine by filtering wastes and extra water from your blood. The urine travels from the kidneys to the bladder in two thin tubes called ureters.
The tube that carries urine from the bladder out of the body.
A walk-in clinic for problems that need care today but are not emergencies, such as minor injuries or infections.
A test of your urine to check for infection, kidney problems, diabetes and more.

Urinary incontinence (UI) is the loss of bladder control, or being unable to control urination. It is a common condition. It can range from being a minor problem to something that greatly affects your daily life.
UTI: an infection in the bladder or urinary tract, causing burning when urinating and needing to go often.
The urinary system is the body's drainage system for removing wastes and extra water. It includes two kidneys, two ureters, a bladder, and a urethra.

Another name for Urinalysis. A urinalysis is a test of your urine. It is often done to check for a urinary tract infection, kidney problems, or diabetes. You may also have one during a checkup, if you are admitted to the hospital, before you have surgery, or if you are pregnant.
Your kidneys make urine by filtering wastes and extra water from your blood. The waste is called urea. Your blood carries it to the kidneys.

Another name for Urinalysis. A urinalysis is a test of your urine. It is often done to check for a urinary tract infection, kidney problems, or diabetes. You may also have one during a checkup, if you are admitted to the hospital, before you have surgery, or if you are pregnant.
A doctor who treats problems of the urinary tract and male reproductive organs.

Another name for Hives. Hives are red and sometimes itchy bumps on your skin. An allergic reaction to a drug or food usually causes them. Allergic reactions cause your body to release chemicals that can make your skin swell up in hives.
Usher syndrome is an inherited disease that causes serious hearing loss and retinitis pigmentosa, an eye disorder that causes your vision to get worse over time.
Another name for Vaginal Bleeding. Bleeding during pregnancy can have several different causes. It is not always serious, but to be safe you should contact your health care provider right away.
Uterine cancer is a cancer that forms in tissues of the uterus, which is sometimes called the womb. The uterus is the place where a fetus grows during pregnancy.
